title: Accounts, sub-accounts & API-key vault
body:
## Context
CandleViewer holds Bybit API keys that can move real money across a main account and up to five sub-accounts, in two environments. E27 is the epic that makes holding them defensible. It is the first epic of the R3 "Trading on demo" train (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7, S14-S15, 2027-03-29 -> 2027-04-23), and the roadmap states its ordering rule as a safety requirement rather than a preference (SS12): "**No order-placing UI ships before** the key vault (E27), risk caps and kill-switch (E39), and the native-SL invariant (E32) are Done." E27 sits on the critical path `E09 -> E27 -> E29 -> E32 -> E34 -> E43 -> E44`, and E28, E29, E39 and E42 all declare it as a dependency.

The epic delivers, per the roadmap's E27 scope line: main and sub-account registration (cap 5, or 20 with Business KYC); envelope encryption of API keys (backend module **M2**) with a KEK held outside the application database and per-key DEKs; key metadata (label, scope, created, last-used, IP whitelist); an automated key self-check calling `GET /v5/user/query-api` that refuses to persist a key with withdrawal permission enabled or without an IP whitelist; key rotation and revocation flows; per-account connectivity health; and the invariant that **keys are never readable back through any API** - only re-entered.

The architecture is already decided and this epic implements it rather than re-litigating it: `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0009-secrets-and-key-management.md` fixes envelope encryption with the KEK in the Windows Credential Manager on the host (a systemd credential or `age`-encrypted file on the later VPS), a DEK per key record, decryption narrowed to a broker used only inside the exchange adapter, blocking start-up assertions, and 90-day rotation with an overlap window. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS3.11 names the components (`AccountAdmin`, `KeyVault`) inside the Admin module (**M13**), and `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2 already contains the DDL for `exchange_accounts`, `api_keys` and `api_key_rotations` including the CHECK constraints that keep withdrawal permission off.

Owner decision #5 is absolute and shapes every ticket here: **withdrawal permission is always OFF, IP allowlisting is always on**. Bybit made the IP allowlist browser-only in February 2026, so it is a manually configured, automatically verified precondition; and new accounts carry a ~48-hour cooldown before keys can be created, which is onboarding lead time the UI must explain rather than a bug to work around.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories covered (domain ACCT, all ten Must/Should stories of `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` SS2):**
- US-ACCT-001 Register a Bybit account (Must) - E27-S01
- US-ACCT-002 Store an API key with envelope encryption (Must) - E27-T02, E27-S02
- US-ACCT-003 API key self-check (Must) - E27-T03, E27-S02
- US-ACCT-004 Key rotation with overlap (Should) - E27-S03
- US-ACCT-005 Key rotation policy reminder (Should) - E27-T04, E27-S03
- US-ACCT-006 Revoke a key immediately (Must) - E27-S04
- US-ACCT-007 Environment binding per account (Must) - E27-T03, E27-S02
- US-ACCT-008 Account balance & margin snapshot (Must) - E27-T04, E27-S05
- US-ACCT-009 Leverage and margin mode control (Must) - E27-S05
- US-ACCT-010 Account health & connection state (Must) - E27-T04, E27-S05

**Screens:** SCR-125 Admin Bybit accounts list, SCR-126 Admin add/edit Bybit account, SCR-127 Admin API key rotation, SCR-128 Admin key health & secrets policy panel, SCR-129 Admin account disable/delete confirmation, SCR-079 Account detail drawer (trading-side); plus the account step of SCR-016 first-run onboarding and the SCR-019 setup checklist card, which this epic updates rather than introduces.

**Components consumed or contributed:** CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge and CMP-176 AccountKeyRow (contributed by this epic's design tickets), plus CMP-001, CMP-011, CMP-027, CMP-028, CMP-033, CMP-034 MaskedValue, CMP-035, CMP-036, CMP-040, CMP-043, CMP-044, CMP-046, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-065, CMP-066 Stepper, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-104 LeverageSlider, CMP-106, CMP-116, CMP-128 MarginModeToggle, CMP-129 PositionModeToggle, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile.

**API surface (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, tag `exchange-accounts`):** `GET|POST /exchange-accounts`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}`, `GET|POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys`, `DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}`, `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}/rotate`, `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}/test`, `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate`, `PATCH /positions/{positionId}/leverage`.

**WS topics (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`):** the private `wallet` topic (account-scoped, 500 ms throttle, whole-object last-write-wins) and the `system` topic's `revoked` reasons `key_revoked`, `account_disabled`, `account_scope_changed`; the `account_scope_denied` error code.

**Database tables (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2):** `exchange_accounts`, `api_keys`, `api_key_rotations`; reads `user_account_access` for scope.

**Backend modules:** **M2** credential broker / key vault (`services/api/candleviewer/credentials/`) and **M13** admin accounts (`services/api/candleviewer/admin/accounts.py`, `keyvault.py`), per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS3.11 and SS5.

**Children:** 1 spike (E27-K01), 5 tasks (E27-T01..T05), 5 stories (E27-S01..S05), 7 design tickets (E27-D01..D07), 5 QA tickets (E27-Q01..Q05), 4 security tickets (E27-X01..X04).

## Out of scope
- **Per-account profiles, trade groups and fan-out** (US-PROF-*) - epic E28; E27 only stores `active_profile_id` and surfaces a profile summary.
- **Order placement, the OMS and the order ticket** - E29, E30, E32; E27 stops at credentials, health and leverage.
- **Risk caps, lockouts and the kill-switch** - E39, even though E27's health states feed them.
- **Users, roles, sessions, TOTP and step-up authentication** - E09; E27 consumes them and asserts their correct application, but does not build them.
- **Audit-log storage, hash-chaining and the audit viewer** - E09/E42; E27 emits events into it.
- **Exchanges other than Bybit and instruments other than USDT linear perpetuals** - out of scope for v1 by the planning brief, though the adapter abstraction is respected.
- **Any Android client and any separate admin application** - out of scope by owner decision 2026-09-14; the admin surfaces are RBAC-gated screens inside the web app.
- **Automating the Bybit IP allowlist** - impossible since February 2026 (browser-only); treated as a verified manual precondition.
- **Deleting keys on Bybit's side as the authoritative action** - CandleViewer attempts it and reports the result, but local deletion is always authoritative.
- **The penetration test and Live enablement gating** - R4, epics E43 and E44.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A database leak alone cannot trade
  Given a Postgres backup of the deployment restored on a machine without access to the KEK
  When the application is started against it
  Then no api_keys row decrypts, the app enters degraded read-only mode with a blocking banner, and every trading route refuses
  And this is the evidence for R3 exit criterion #9 "KEK separation demonstrated"

Scenario: A key that can withdraw is never stored
  Given an operator submits an API key whose permissions include Wallet/Withdraw
  When the mandatory verification pipeline runs
  Then the key is rejected with validation_failed / key_withdraw_permission before anything is persisted, the reason is displayed verbatim, and the account cannot be marked trading-enabled
  And this is the evidence for R3 exit criterion #10

Scenario: No secret is readable back, anywhere
  Given keys have been stored for every registered account
  When every REST route, every WS topic, every log stream, the metrics endpoint, traces, error bodies and a generated support bundle are searched for the stored secrets
  Then none of them contains any secret material, and no reveal control exists in any screen

Scenario: The owner can run the whole account lifecycle unaided
  Given a fresh deployment
  When the owner registers a main account and a sub-account, imports and verifies keys, observes health and balances, changes leverage, rotates a key with overlap, and revokes a key after a suspected compromise
  Then every step succeeds using only the shipped UI and the runbooks, and the audit trail reconstructs the entire sequence with the actor, the outcome and key fingerprints only

Scenario: A manager cannot reach an account they were not granted
  Given a manager session granted account A only
  When the manager requests account B over REST and subscribes to wallet for B over WS
  Then REST answers 403 without revealing whether B exists, the WS subscription is refused with account_scope_denied, and both attempts are audited

Scenario: An account that cannot be reached cannot be traded
  Given neither the private WS nor REST has succeeded for an account for 30 seconds
  Then the account's health shows red within the deadline, order entry is disabled for it, the state is announced to assistive technology, and the dead-man's-switch policy is invoked

Scenario: The epic closes with all three signatures
  When E27 is proposed for Done
  Then QA sign-off (E27-Q05), Security sign-off (E27-X04) and design sign-off (E27-D07) are all recorded, zero P0/P1 defects are open, coverage is at least 90% on the credential and accounts modules, and no Critical or High security finding is outstanding

## Technical notes / design
**Sequencing.** Design runs two sprints ahead: E27-D01..D06 execute in S12-S13 so that every screen is signed off before S14 opens, satisfying the design-ahead rule. Engineering in S14 is backend-only and bottom-up - E27-K01 settles KEK custody, E27-T01 lands the schema, E27-T02 builds the M2 credential broker on top of it, E27-T03 adds the verification pipeline; in parallel E27-X01 produces the threat model that E27-T02 and E27-T03 must satisfy, and E27-Q01 writes the black-box plan and the fault-injection fixtures. S15 delivers the five stories on the frontend, the health monitor (E27-T04), the runbooks (E27-T05) and the whole QA and security closing sequence.

**Envelope encryption (ADR-0009).** Each `api_keys` row carries its own AES-256-GCM DEK; the DEK is wrapped by the KEK and stored as `dek_ref` with `kek_version`; the row holds `secret_enc`, `enc_nonce` and the auth tag. Rotating the KEK bumps `kek_version` and rewraps DEKs without touching ciphertext - `ix_api_keys_kek` exists precisely to drive that job. Plaintext exists only inside the credential broker, only for the lifetime of a request signature, wrapped in a type whose string representations return a mask.

**Verification pipeline (the epic's safety core).** `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys` persists nothing until every check passes: `GET /v5/user/query-api`; `permissions.Wallet` must not contain `Withdraw`; required scopes present for a trade key; `unified` true and the UID equal to `exchange_accounts.exchange_uid`; a non-empty IP allowlist containing the deployment egress IP when `require_ip_whitelist` is set (default true for live); expiry at least 14 days away or a warning attached; and a signed no-op `wallet-balance` probe returning `retCode=0` inside `recv_window`, which also validates clock sync. The full result is stored as `permission_snapshot` and re-checked every boot and every six hours, with the live response always overriding the stored snapshot.

**Environment binding.** `exchange_accounts.env` participates in client selection for every outbound request; there is no fallback from demo to live under any failure condition. Demo has no WS order entry, so the demo path is REST for order placement while private streams remain WS.

**Health model.** Green when the private WS is connected and authenticated with a heartbeat under 10 s; amber when WS has dropped and REST polling has taken over, with sub-second rule actions flagged; red within 30 s when neither succeeds, disabling order entry and invoking the dead-man's-switch. Balances are WS-first with a REST truth-check after 60 s of silence, and no figure is ever rendered without a freshness indicator.

**Risks carried by this epic (`docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`).** R10 key-person / key-custody - the KEK is a single point of failure for starting the service, accepted in ADR-0009 with an owner-held offline backup and a runbook; R13 sharing abuse - a manager reaching accounts they were not granted, mitigated by server-side scope derivation and the E27-X03 matrix; R7 data accuracy - a stale balance or health state presented as current, mitigated by structural freshness pairing; R11 alert reliability - a self-check failure that never reaches the owner, drilled in E27-X04; R3 real-time cost - a self-check storm consuming the per-UID exchange budget and starving the order path, measured in E27-Q03.

## Test plan
Epic-level verification is the epic-level end-to-end pass in **E27-Q05** plus the drills in **E27-X04**, not the sum of the children's tests. The children carry their own unit, contract, integration, E2E, load, chaos and accessibility plans:
- Unit and contract: E27-T01..T05, E27-S01..S05, with coverage at least 90% on the credential and accounts modules (M2 is in the roadmap's >=90% list) and at least 80% frontend.
- Black-box plan and fault-injection fixtures: E27-Q01. Automated E2E: E27-Q02. Load, soak and chaos: E27-Q03. Accessibility audit and exploratory charters: E27-Q04. Regression pack and sign-off: E27-Q05.
- Security: leak-assertion suite and abuse-case execution in E27-X02, RBAC and scope matrix in E27-X03, restore/rotation/KEK-rotation/compromise drills in E27-X04.

## Security notes
E27 is the epic where the security program is the product. Controls that must exist when it closes: KEK custody outside the database and outside WSL (ADR-0009, drilled in E27-X04); DEK per key record with GCM authentication; decryption narrowed to the credential broker with a masking wrapper type; blocking start-up assertions for withdrawal-off and IP-allowlist presence; secrets never returned by any API, never logged, never traced, never in metrics, error bodies or support bundles, asserted by a required CI check; server-side account-scope derivation on every REST route and WS subscription; step-up authentication on every state-changing key action; hash-chained audit entries recording fingerprints only.

Data classification, fixed by E27-X01 and cited by every child: `secret_enc`, `enc_nonce`, `dek_ref` and the KEK are **Secret**; `exchange_uid`, `label`, `permission_snapshot`, balances and fee rates are **Confidential**; health states are **Internal**.

The epic carries the `security` label. STRIDE (E27-X01) is a gating deliverable, security review (E27-X02) and the RBAC matrix (E27-X03) are required checks, and the R3 gate cannot pass with any Critical or High finding open (roadmap SS7.4).

## Accessibility notes
Six screens, all WCAG 2.2 AA. The epic's distinctive accessibility requirement is that safety verdicts must be perceivable without colour and announced when they change: the withdrawal-permission failure on SCR-125/126 is text plus icon and rendered as a blocking error rather than a warning; the SCR-126 test result is a list, not a colour; the SCR-127 rotation stepper marks progress with `aria-current="step"` and labelled step regions; SCR-129 is a `role="alertdialog"` restating consequences as a list with typed confirmation and focus starting on Cancel; account health transitions are announced through a live region (US-ACCT-010 NFR); secret inputs are `type=password` with an explicit "value is write-only" description and no reveal control. Design-time review is E27-D05, the built-product audit is E27-Q04, and axe-core runs in CI with serious/critical violations failing the build.

## Performance notes
This epic is not throughput-critical but it is latency-visible and budget-sensitive. Targets from the screen specs and `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: the SCR-126 validation round-trip <=3 s; SCR-127 rotation <=10 s end to end; SCR-079 drawer opening <=100 ms from cached state; SCR-125/128 health computed server-side, cached 60 s and never refreshed per second; the `wallet` WS topic throttled at 500 ms with whole-object last-write-wins. The hard constraint is the per-UID exchange rate budget (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS4.3): verification and health polling must never consume the share reserved for order placement, which E27-Q03 measures directly.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_account_health_state{account,env}`, `cv_key_verification_total{result}`, `cv_key_age_days{account,key}`, `cv_credential_borrow_total{result}`, `cv_kek_load_failures_total`, `cv_exchange_rate_limit_remaining{uid}`, plus authorisation-denial counts by route and role. Audit events (hash-chained, fingerprints only): `account.created`, `account.updated`, `account.tested`, `account.key_rotated`, `account.disabled`, `account.deleted`, `account.disabled_by_policy`, `admin.key_marked_compromised`, `admin.secrets_policy_changed`. Analytics: `account.detail_viewed`, `admin.key_health_viewed`. Alerts: self-check failing, account red for over 60 s, KEK load failure, key overdue for rotation - each verified to actually reach the owner's notification channel during the E27-X04 drills, since an alert that fires into a void is a finding.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All 26 children Done (100% rollup) or explicitly descoped with a recorded Won't/Later disposition on this epic.
- [ ] The seven epic-level acceptance scenarios above verified end to end, not inferred from child tickets.
- [ ] R3 exit criteria #9 (KEK separation demonstrated) and #10 (withdrawal-enabled keys refused) evidenced with dated artefacts from this train.
- [ ] Coverage: >=90% on `candleviewer/credentials` and `candleviewer/admin/accounts`, >=85% backend elsewhere, >=80% frontend; no open P0/P1 defects against E27.
- [ ] Docs reflect shipped behaviour: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` deltas noted; ADR-0009 amended (E27-T05); operator, rotation and compromise runbooks published under `docs/ops/runbooks/`.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green in CI on all six screens and at least one manual screen-reader pass recorded (E27-Q04).
- [ ] perf: budgets measured and recorded against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (E27-Q03).
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, all Critical/High closed, Security-engineer sign-off recorded (E27-X01, E27-X02, E27-X03, E27-X04).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded from the epic-level regression and exploratory pass (E27-Q05).
- [ ] Design sign-off recorded, design QA drift report filed (E27-D07).
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review with acceptance recorded, showing the full account lifecycle on demo.
- [ ] Retro note captured; any process learnings filed as Chore tickets.
- [ ] Downstream epics E28, E29, E39 and E42 formally unblocked.

## Dependencies
**Blocked by E09** (Auth, sessions, 2FA & RBAC): E27 consumes roles and permissions (`accounts:read`, `accounts:write`, `keys:read`, `keys:manage`), `user_account_access` scope resolution, step-up authentication for every state-changing key action, and the hash-chained append-only audit log. None of E27's safety properties are meaningful without them, which is why the roadmap's critical path starts `E09 -> E27`.

**Interfaces relied on:** the exchange adapter protocol in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS14 (Bybit REST and private WS clients, environment-aware host selection, the `10018` rate-limit error path); the WS gateway's scope-checked subscription manager for the `wallet` topic; the Permission enum in SS15.2; the settings model for `require_ip_whitelist`, `CV_KEK_SOURCE` and `CV_ENV`.

**Blocks:** E28 (per-account profiles and trade groups need accounts and profile binding), E29 (the OMS needs credentials and account health), E39 (risk caps and the kill-switch consume account health), E42 (admin screens extend the shell and the accounts surfaces), and transitively E32, E34, E43 and E44 along the critical path.

## Branch
`feat/e27-accounts-key-vault` as the epic umbrella; each child uses its own `feat/e27-<short>`, `design/e27-<short>` or `chore/e27-<short>` branch as stated on the ticket. PRs stay at or under 400 LOC diff, with 2 approvals including 1 code-owner; the credential broker, the verification pipeline and anything touching `api_keys` additionally require Security-engineer review per CODEOWNERS.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. title: Spike: KEK custody, injection and rotation for the WSL and VPS deployments
body:
## Context
ADR-0009 (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0009-secrets-and-key-management.md`) decides envelope encryption with a 256-bit KEK stored in the **Windows Credential Manager on the host**, injected into `cv-api` at process start by a small host-side launcher, with `CV_KEK_SOURCE=file` available for development only and refusing to start when `CV_ENV=live`. The ADR itself flags the launcher as bespoke tooling that must work on Windows today and on a VPS later (systemd credential or an `age`-encrypted file with restrictive permissions).

Every other ticket in E27 depends on a working KEK loader, and R3 exit criterion #9 requires that "DB compromise alone is insufficient to decrypt keys (KEK separation demonstrated)". This timeboxed spike removes the remaining unknowns - injection mechanism, unattended restart, rotation semantics and the degraded-mode contract - before E27-T02 builds the credential broker.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Timeboxed investigation: 3 working days, 1 engineer (backend) with the Security engineer consulted, producing `docs/ops/runbooks/kek-custody.md` and an amendment note appended to ADR-0009.
- Prototype the host-side launcher: read the KEK from Windows Credential Manager and hand it to the WSL `docker compose` process as a process-scoped secret - never a file inside WSL, never a compose `environment:` entry visible through `docker inspect`.
- Prototype and measure three injection mechanisms, then recommend one: (a) `docker compose run --env` driven by the launcher, (b) Compose `secrets:` backed by a pipe, (c) an authenticated localhost unwrap call from `cv-api` to the host launcher at start-up.
- Specify the VPS variant: systemd `LoadCredential=` versus an `age`-encrypted file at `0600`, including unattended-restart semantics (ADR-0009 rejects a password prompt at start-up because recovery must work while positions are open).
- Define `kek_version` semantics against `api_keys.kek_version` and the re-wrap job that bumps DEK wrapping on KEK rotation without touching ciphertext (`ix_api_keys_kek` exists for exactly this).
- Define the degraded-mode contract consumed by E27-T02 and E27-S02: US-ACCT-002 scenario "KEK unavailable" - the app starts read-only, shows a blocking banner and refuses all trading routes.
- Write the restore drill: restore a Postgres backup on a machine without the KEK and prove that nothing decrypts.
- Fix the configuration vocabulary: `CV_KEK_SOURCE`, `CV_KEK_HANDLE`, `CV_KEK_VERSION`, `CV_ENV`.

## Out of scope
Implementing the credential broker (E27-T02); Vault/OpenBao and cloud KMS (both rejected in ADR-0009 and not to be re-litigated); TOTP-secret storage (owned by E09, which reuses the same envelope pattern); backup and restore tooling itself (owned by E22).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One injection mechanism is chosen with evidence
  Given all three candidate mechanisms have been prototyped
  When the spike closes
  Then exactly one is recommended, with measured start-up latency, a written statement of where the KEK is visible (process environment, /proc, docker inspect, WSL filesystem) and a reason for rejecting each alternative

Scenario: The KEK is not recoverable from inside the container
  Given the recommended mechanism is running
  When an operator runs `docker inspect`, reads /proc/1/environ from a sibling container and greps every mounted WSL volume
  Then the KEK value appears in none of them, evidenced by a recorded terminal transcript attached to the ticket

Scenario: Unattended restart succeeds
  Given the host reboots while open positions exist in Postgres
  When the stack restarts with no human present
  Then cv-api obtains the KEK and reaches Running without any interactive prompt

Scenario: A missing KEK degrades safely
  Given the configured KEK source is unavailable
  When cv-api starts
  Then it reaches Degraded, order-entry routes return 403, a critical alert is raised, and the exact remediation text is written to the log

Scenario: The spike is inconclusive
  Given no mechanism satisfies both non-visibility and unattended restart
  When the timebox expires
  Then the gap is recorded, a follow-up ticket is raised, and the least-bad interim option is proposed together with a compensating control
```

## Technical notes / design
Threat framing for the evaluation: the attacker holds a Postgres dump and/or read access to the WSL filesystem, but not the host console. Score each mechanism on KEK-at-rest location, KEK-in-transit path, process visibility, auditability and failure mode.

Key hierarchy to validate against `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md#322-api_keys`: the row stores `key_id_enc` and `secret_enc` (AES-256-GCM ciphertext), `enc_nonce` (12 bytes, `ak_nonce_len` CHECK), `enc_alg = 'AES-256-GCM'` (`ak_alg` CHECK), `dek_ref` (keyring handle of the wrapped DEK) and `kek_version >= 1` (`ak_kek_pos` CHECK). A KEK rotation therefore only rewraps DEKs and bumps `kek_version`; ciphertext is untouched.

Hard rule to specify: `CV_KEK_SOURCE=file` together with `CV_ENV=live` must be a fatal start-up failure with error code `kek_source_not_permitted`.

## Test plan
No production code ships from a spike. The deliverables are evidence: transcripts of the non-visibility checks, a timing table of start-up latency per mechanism, and the restore-drill log. The throwaway prototype lives on `spike/e27-kek-custody` and is deleted after the write-up; only documentation merges to `main`.

## Security notes
This spike *is* the security control that makes the vault meaningful. KEK classification: **Secret, highest tier**. Threats addressed, expanded formally in E27-X01: information disclosure through a database dump, through container inspection and through the WSL filesystem; elevation of privilege when a development-mode file source leaks into a live deployment. Requires the `security` label and Security-engineer acceptance of the recommendation before E27-T02 starts.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface is produced by this spike. The degraded-mode banner it specifies is designed in E27-D03 and built in E27-S02.

## Performance notes
KEK acquisition must add <=500 ms to `cv-api` boot; the measured figure per mechanism goes in the timing table. The re-wrap job must process the entire `api_keys` table (<=50 rows in v1: main plus up to 5 subs, live and demo, plus rotation history) in <=5 s.

## Observability
Specify - not implement - the metrics E27-T02 will emit: `cv_kek_load_seconds` (histogram), `cv_kek_load_failures_total{reason}` (counter), `cv_kek_version` (gauge). Specify the audit event names `security.kek_loaded`, `security.kek_load_failed`, `security.kek_rotated`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Timebox of 3 days respected; findings written up in `docs/ops/runbooks/kek-custody.md` plus an ADR-0009 amendment note.
- [ ] Recommendation reviewed and accepted by both the Security engineer and the Architect.
- [ ] Evidence artefacts attached: non-visibility transcripts, start-up timing table, restore-drill log.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets raised for anything deliberately deferred.
- [ ] E27-T02 is unblocked: injection mechanism, config keys, degraded-mode contract and re-wrap semantics are all specified unambiguously.
- [ ] Prototype branch deleted; no prototype code merged.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09** (auth, sessions, 2FA and RBAC) because degraded-mode route gating and step-up authentication are defined there and this spike must specify how trading routes are refused. Relies on the `AppContext` injection and module-lifecycle contract from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS6, delivered by E02 in R0.

title: Land exchange_accounts, api_keys and api_key_rotations migrations and domain models
body:
## Context
E27 is the first epic that persists exchange identity and credential material. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2 already specifies the DDL verbatim; this task lands it as an Alembic migration plus pydantic v2 domain models in the accounts module, so every later E27 ticket writes against a frozen schema instead of inventing columns.

The DDL is not negotiable: it encodes the epic's safety invariants as database constraints - `ak_no_withdraw CHECK (can_withdraw = false)`, `ux_api_keys_active` (exactly one active key per account), `ea_parent_shape`, and trigger `trg_ea_env_parent` (a sub-account's `env` must equal its parent's). Those constraints are the last line of defence if application logic is ever bypassed, and the schema doc states why cross-env parenting matters: it "would let a demo key fan out into a live group".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating enums `account_kind` and `key_status` (and reusing `exchange_env` from the E09 chain) and tables `exchange_accounts`, `api_keys`, `api_key_rotations` exactly as specified in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md#32-exchange-accounts-api-keys-profiles`.
- Every named constraint and index: `ea_parent_shape`, `ea_no_self_parent`, `ea_acct_type`, `ux_ea_uid`, `ux_ea_label`, `ix_ea_parent`, `ix_ea_tradeable`; `ak_no_withdraw`, `ak_alg`, `ak_nonce_len`, `ak_last4`, `ak_readonly_excl`, `ak_kek_pos`, `ak_snapshot_shape`, `ux_api_keys_label`, `ux_api_keys_active`, `ix_api_keys_rotation`, `ix_api_keys_kek`.
- Trigger `trg_ea_env_parent` enforcing that a sub-account's `env` equals its parent's `env`.
- `COMMENT ON COLUMN` markers for `api_keys.secret_enc` and `api_keys.key_id_enc` recording them as SECRET, per the schema document.
- Package `services/api/candleviewer/accounts/` following the module conventions in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS3: `__init__.py` exporting only the public interface, `models.py` (`ExchangeAccount`, `ApiKeyMetadata`, `ApiKeyRotation`, `PermissionSnapshot`), `errors.py`, `service.py` implementing `start(ctx)` / `stop(grace_s)` / `health()`.
- Repository layer with typed queries. **No model exposes `secret_enc`, `key_id_enc`, `enc_nonce` or `dek_ref` in any serialisable shape** - those columns are read only by the credential broker's internal row type (E27-T02).
- Debounced `last_used_at` writer (at most one write per key per minute - the write-amplification guard named in the schema doc).
- Seed fixtures under `packages/fixtures/accounts/`: one `main`/`live` account, one `sub`/`live` account, one `demo` account, each with a compliant `permission_snapshot`.
- A clean down-migration.

## Out of scope
Credential encryption and decryption (E27-T02); the `account_profiles`, `trade_groups` and `trade_group_legs` tables (owned by E28); `user_account_access` (owned by E09); any REST route (E27-S01 onward).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and rolls back
  Given a database at the previous Alembic revision
  When `alembic upgrade head` runs and then `alembic downgrade -1`
  Then both complete without error and the schema returns exactly to the previous revision

Scenario: Withdrawal permission cannot be persisted
  Given an insert into api_keys with can_withdraw = true
  When the statement executes
  Then Postgres rejects it as a violation of constraint ak_no_withdraw

Scenario: Only one active key per account
  Given an account that already has a key with status 'active' and revoked_at NULL
  When a second active key for the same account is inserted
  Then unique index ux_api_keys_active rejects it

Scenario: Cross-environment parenting is rejected
  Given a main account with env = 'live'
  When a sub-account with env = 'demo' is inserted pointing at it as parent
  Then trigger trg_ea_env_parent raises and the insert fails

Scenario: The permission snapshot must prove withdrawal is empty
  When a permission_snapshot whose permissions.Withdraw array is non-empty is inserted
  Then constraint ak_snapshot_shape rejects the row

Scenario: Duplicate UID per environment is rejected
  Given a row with exchange='bybit', env='live', exchange_uid='10234567' and deleted_at NULL
  When another row with the same triple is inserted
  Then ux_ea_uid rejects it

Scenario: Secret columns are unreachable from domain models
  When ExchangeAccount.model_dump() and ApiKeyMetadata.model_dump() are inspected
  Then neither contains secret_enc, key_id_enc, enc_nonce or dek_ref
```

## Technical notes / design
The Alembic revision follows the R0 naming convention (`{epoch}_{slug}`) and is **additive only**, so it can be deployed ahead of the routes with no coupling.

Domain-model rules:
- `PermissionSnapshot` mirrors the JSON shape documented in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md#322-api_keys`: `fetched_at`, `uid`, `note`, `readOnly`, `permissions` (`ContractTrade`, `Spot`, `Wallet`, `Options`, `Derivatives`, `Exchange`, `NFT`, `Withdraw`), `ips`, `type`, `expiredAt`. A model validator asserts `permissions.Withdraw` is empty, so the failure surfaces as the documented `validation_failed` / `key_withdraw_permission` problem rather than a 500 from a Postgres CHECK.
- `key_id_last4` is the only key-derived value that may ever be rendered. The API field `key_id_masked` is composed at import time as `first4...last4`; outside import only `...{key_id_last4}` is available, because the first four characters are never persisted.
- `last_used_at` debounce is implemented in the repository (in-memory last-write timestamp per key), not as a database trigger, so it stays testable and cheap.

Error codes reused from the OpenAPI `Problem` registry: `validation_failed`, `conflict`, `not_found`.

## Test plan
Unit: model validators (non-empty Withdraw rejected; nonce length; `read_only` and `can_trade` mutually exclusive); repository round-trip per table; `last_used_at` debounce window.
Migration tests: upgrade then downgrade against a scratch Postgres in CI.
Constraint matrix: one parameterised test per named constraint (19 of them) that crafts a violating row and asserts the specific constraint name appears in the raised error - this is what proves the invariants are real and not merely declared.
Fixtures: `packages/fixtures/accounts/`.
Coverage target >=90% on `candleviewer/accounts/`.

## Security notes
Data classification: `secret_enc`, `key_id_enc`, `enc_nonce`, `dek_ref` are **Secret**; `exchange_uid`, `label` and `permission_snapshot` are **Confidential**. Threat addressed here: an over-broad ORM model accidentally serialising ciphertext into an API response, a log line or a support bundle - prevented structurally by never placing those columns on a serialisable model, and asserted by the model_dump test above. Detailed STRIDE analysis is E27-X01; this ticket does not itself need a security review label.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface.

## Performance notes
The account list is at most 6 rows in v1 (main plus up to 5 subs per environment), so index design is about correctness rather than throughput. The exception is `ix_ea_tradeable`, the hot path used by trade-group leg selection in E34; it must be created as the specified partial index. The migration must complete in under 2 s on an empty database.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_accounts_rows{env,kind}` and `cv_api_keys_rows{status}` gauges, published by the accounts module `health()` and scraped by Prometheus. INFO log on migration apply with the revision id. No audit events in this ticket - audit rows are emitted by the routes in E27-S01 onward.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via PR <=400 LOC diff, conventional commits, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner; all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/accounts` and `candleviewer/credentials` (M2 is in the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; no field shipped that is not in the spec, no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: schema/API deltas noted in the PR description; runbook entry added when the change is operational.
- [ ] Observability (metrics, audit events) added and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off (E27-D06 handoff accepted, E27-D07 design QA passed) for any ticket touching UI.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E27-Q05.

title: Build the M2 credential broker: envelope encryption, KEK loader and degraded mode
body:
## Context
Module **M2** is the only place in CandleViewer where API-key plaintext exists. ADR-0009 fixes the design: a per-record AES-256-GCM DEK encrypts the credential, the DEK is wrapped by a KEK held outside the database, and "plaintext keys exist only inside the exchange adapter, only for the lifetime of a request signature, and are held in a wrapper type whose `__repr__`/`__str__` return `***`". R3 exit criterion #9 requires that no API path returns a secret and that a database compromise alone cannot decrypt keys. US-ACCT-002 is the user-facing statement of the same requirement.

This task builds that broker, so that key import (E27-T03), rotation (E27-S03), revocation (E27-S04) and every signing call site in the exchange adapter go through one narrow, audited interface.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Module `services/api/candleviewer/credentials/` (M2) exposing exactly four public operations: `store(...)`, `with_credentials(key_id, fn)` (a scoped borrow), `destroy(key_id)` and `rewrap_all(new_kek_version)`. There is deliberately **no** `get_secret()` in the public interface.
- `Secret[str]` wrapper type: `__repr__`, `__str__` and `__format__` return `***`; `model_dump()` raises; pickling raises; the type is excluded by the structured-logging allow-list serialiser and by the tracer attribute filter.
- KEK loader implementing the mechanism chosen in E27-K01, driven by `CV_KEK_SOURCE` (`credman|systemd|file`), `CV_KEK_HANDLE` and `CV_KEK_VERSION`, with a fatal start-up failure `kek_source_not_permitted` when `CV_KEK_SOURCE=file` and `CV_ENV=live`.
- Envelope encryption: DEK from `os.urandom(32)`, wrapped under the KEK; a fresh 12-byte GCM nonce per encryption; writes `key_id_enc`, `secret_enc`, `enc_nonce`, `enc_alg`, `dek_ref`, `kek_version` and `key_id_last4` into `api_keys`.
- KEK-rotation re-wrap job: iterate `api_keys` via `ix_api_keys_kek`, unwrap with the old KEK, rewrap under the new, bump `kek_version`; ciphertext untouched; idempotent and resumable after a kill.
- **Degraded mode** implementing US-ACCT-002 scenario 3: when the KEK cannot be loaded at start-up the app enters `Degraded` per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS6, all trading routes return `403`, the WS `system` topic publishes the degraded health state, and a critical alert fires.
- Registration of the secret types with the allow-list log serialiser, the Problem-body builder, the OpenTelemetry attribute filter and the support-bundle exporter.
- In-memory unwrapped-DEK cache keyed by `key_id` with a 5-minute TTL, flushed on revoke, rotate and KEK rotation.

## Out of scope
REST routes (E27-T03 and E27-S01 onward); Bybit request signing itself (the exchange adapter, owned by E08); TOTP-secret storage (E09 reuses this pattern but is not in scope here); backup and restore tooling (E22).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A secret is never renderable
  Given a Secret wrapping the value "topsecret"
  When it is interpolated into an f-string, repr()-ed, logged through structlog, serialised into a Problem body, attached to a trace span and written into a support bundle
  Then the literal "topsecret" appears in none of those outputs and "***" appears instead

Scenario: Envelope round-trip
  Given a stored key
  When with_credentials borrows it
  Then the plaintext matches what was stored, and after the callback returns the broker holds no reference to the plaintext buffer

Scenario: The database alone is not enough
  Given a complete dump of the api_keys table and no KEK
  When decryption is attempted using only the dump
  Then it fails, proven by an automated test that runs the broker against the dump with a deliberately absent KEK handle

Scenario: KEK unavailable at start-up
  Given CV_KEK_SOURCE points at a handle that cannot be read
  When cv-api starts
  Then the app reports Degraded, POST /api/v1/orders returns 403, the WS system topic carries the degraded notice, and a critical alert is raised

Scenario: File KEK source is refused in live
  Given CV_KEK_SOURCE=file and CV_ENV=live
  When cv-api starts
  Then it exits non-zero with kek_source_not_permitted and no credential is decrypted

Scenario: KEK rotation rewraps without touching ciphertext
  Given 20 stored keys at kek_version 1
  When rewrap_all runs for KEK version 2
  Then every row has kek_version 2 and an updated dek_ref, secret_enc is byte-identical to before, and every key still decrypts

Scenario: The rewrap job is resumable
  Given the job is killed after 8 of 20 rows
  When it is restarted
  Then it completes the remaining rows and leaves no row in a mixed or undecryptable state

Scenario: A wrong KEK fails loudly
  Given a key wrapped under KEK version 1
  When a borrow is attempted with KEK version 2 material
  Then the GCM authentication tag check fails and the error is surfaced, never a silently wrong plaintext
```

## Technical notes / design
Public interface:

```python
class CredentialBroker(Protocol):
    async def store(self, account_id: UUID, label: str,
                    api_key: Secret[str], api_secret: Secret[str]) -> ApiKeyMetadata: ...
    async def with_credentials(self, key_id: UUID,
                               fn: Callable[[Secret[str], Secret[str]], Awaitable[T]]) -> T: ...
    async def destroy(self, key_id: UUID) -> None: ...
    async def rewrap_all(self, new_kek_version: int) -> RewrapReport: ...
```

`with_credentials` is a *scoped borrow* precisely so that no caller can hold plaintext beyond its signing call - that is what turns ADR-0009 item 3 from an aspiration into an enforceable property. Every borrow writes the audit row `security.credential_borrowed {key_id, caller_module, purpose}` and updates `last_used_at` through the debounced repository path from E27-T01.

Nonce discipline: a fresh `os.urandom(12)` nonce per encryption, never reused when a row is re-encrypted. The `ak_nonce_len` CHECK guards length; a unit test guards uniqueness across 10^5 generations.

Degraded-mode wiring: the broker's `health()` returns red when the KEK is absent; the supervisor maps red health on M2 to the `Degraded` app state; the gateway's trading-route dependency then raises `403` with code `forbidden` and a detail naming the KEK; and the `system` WS topic publishes `health: "degraded"` per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS9.

Config keys: `CV_KEK_SOURCE`, `CV_KEK_HANDLE`, `CV_KEK_VERSION`, `CV_ENV`, `CV_DEK_CACHE_TTL_S` (default 300).
Error codes: `kek_source_not_permitted` (start-up, fatal), `credential_unavailable` (borrow failed), `forbidden` (trading route while degraded).

## Test plan
Unit: the `Secret` leak matrix (repr / str / format / structlog / json / pickle / trace attribute / Problem body); envelope round-trip; nonce uniqueness; wrong-KEK authentication-tag failure; DEK cache TTL and flush-on-revoke.
Integration: the broker against a real Postgres carrying the E27-T01 schema; the rewrap job over 50 seeded rows including a kill-and-resume cycle.
Chaos: remove the KEK handle while the process is running - the next borrow must fail closed and the app must degrade rather than serve stale plaintext.
Security test, wired as a **required check**: the ADR-0009 validation item "a crafted log line containing a key value is asserted absent from stdout, files and the metrics endpoint". Implemented here and reused by E27-X02.
Restore drill automated in CI: restore the fixture dump with no KEK present and assert zero successful decryptions.
Coverage target >=90% (M2 is named in the roadmap's >=90% module list).

## Security notes
This is the epic's highest-value control. STRIDE summary, expanded in E27-X01: **Information disclosure** - database dump, log leak, trace leak, support bundle, metric label, exception body, core dump; **Tampering** - ciphertext substitution, defeated by the GCM authentication tag; **Elevation of privilege** - a development file KEK source reaching a live deployment, blocked by the start-up assertion; **Repudiation** - defeated because every borrow is audited to the hash-chained audit log. Data classification: Secret. Plaintext must never reach disk, including temporary files and core dumps - `ulimit -c 0` is documented in the runbook. **This ticket requires the `security` label and explicit Security-engineer review before merge.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. The degraded-mode banner this ticket triggers is designed in E27-D03 and implemented in E27-S02.

## Performance notes
KEK load must add <=500 ms to boot (budget set in E27-K01). A credential borrow (unwrap DEK plus decrypt) must be <=2 ms p99, because it sits inside the order-submit path whose p95 budget is 300 ms (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, budget #4, and R3 exit criterion #11). Benchmark the borrow with and without the DEK cache and record both figures in the PR.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_kek_load_seconds`, `cv_kek_load_failures_total{reason}`, `cv_kek_version`, `cv_credential_borrow_seconds`, `cv_credential_borrow_total{module,result}`, `cv_credential_rewrap_rows_total`, `cv_dek_cache_hits_total`.
Audit events, appended to the hash-chained audit log: `security.kek_loaded`, `security.kek_load_failed`, `security.kek_rotated`, `security.credential_stored`, `security.credential_borrowed`, `security.credential_destroyed`.
Logs carry `key_id`, `exchange_account_id`, `kek_version` and `caller_module` - never key material. One trace span per borrow, with attributes restricted to the allow-list.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via PR <=400 LOC diff, conventional commits, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner; all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/accounts` and `candleviewer/credentials` (M2 is in the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; no field shipped that is not in the spec, no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: schema/API deltas noted in the PR description; runbook entry added when the change is operational.
- [ ] Observability (metrics, audit events) added and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off (E27-D06 handoff accepted, E27-D07 design QA passed) for any ticket touching UI.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E27-Q05.
- [ ] Secret-leak assertion suite from E27-T02/E27-X02 passes: no key material in logs, traces, metrics, error bodies or support bundles.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-K01** (injection mechanism, config vocabulary, degraded contract) and **E27-T01** (tables and models). Relies on the `AppContext` dependency injection and module-lifecycle contract from E02, and on the degraded-state route gating defined in E09.

- REST routes (E27-T03 and E27-S01 onward); Bybit request signing itself (the exchange adapter, owned by E08); TOTP-secret storage (E09 reuses this pattern but is not in scope here); backup and restore tooling (E22).
- No per-tick/hot-path logic moved into a statechart action or service (docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md §1.2).

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

title: Implement the mandatory API-key verification pipeline and the key self-check service
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` specifies a **mandatory verification pipeline** on `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys`: the key is persisted only if all seven checks pass, the most important being that `permissions.Wallet` must not contain `Withdraw` (owner decision #5 in the planning brief), that the UID matches `exchange_accounts.exchange_uid`, that the account is UTA, that an IP whitelist is present and contains the deployment egress IP, and that a signed no-op probe returns `retCode=0` inside the `recv_window` (which doubles as a clock-sync check).

US-ACCT-003 makes the same pipeline a recurring self-check ("every boot and every 6 h"), and US-ACCT-007 adds environment binding: a live key pasted into a demo-bound account must fail with "key does not belong to this environment", and there is never a silent fallback between hosts. R3 exit criterion #9 requires that every key in the system is verified withdrawal-OFF and IP-whitelisted by this automated self-check.

This task builds the pipeline once, as a service, so that key import, `POST .../keys/{keyId}/test`, the boot assertion and the 6-hourly job all execute exactly the same checks.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `candleviewer/accounts/verification.py` implementing `verify(candidate_or_stored, account, include_ws: bool) -> VerificationResult` with the seven checks from the OpenAPI description, in order:
  1. `GET /v5/user/query-api` with the credentials.
  2. `permissions.Wallet` must not contain `Withdraw`; failure returns `validation_failed` with `rule: key_withdraw_permission`.
  3. Required scopes present - `ContractTrade` with `Order` and `Position` for a trade key; a read-only key must have none of them and is stored with `read_only: true`.
  4. `unified` must be true (UTA) and the UID must equal `exchange_accounts.exchange_uid`.
  5. IP whitelist must be non-empty when `require_ip_whitelist` is set in settings (default true for `live`), and the deployment egress IP must be inside it.
  6. If an expiry is set it must be at least 14 days away, otherwise a warning is attached.
  7. A signed no-op probe `GET /v5/account/wallet-balance` must return `retCode=0` within the `recv_window`.
- `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys` wired to the pipeline plus the E27-T02 broker: verify first, persist only on success, return `ApiKeyWithVerification` exactly as specified (`key` plus `verification` with `passed`, `uid`, `unified`, `permissions`, `withdraw_enabled`, `ip_whitelist`, `ip_whitelist_matches_egress`, `clock_offset_ms`, `probe_ret_code`, `warnings`). `x-idempotency: required`, permission `keys:manage`, scope `none`.
- `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}/test` returning `KeyTestResult` (`passed`, `checked_at`, `rest{ok,latency_ms,ret_code}`, `websocket{ok,error}`, `verification`), with `include_ws` defaulting to true; **a failed probe is still HTTP 200 with `passed: false`**, per the spec. Permission `keys:read`, scope `granted_accounts`. This endpoint never places an order.
- Environment binding (US-ACCT-007): host selection is derived from `exchange_accounts.env`; `live` uses the live REST and private WS hosts, `demo` uses `api-demo.bybit.com` and the demo private WS. There is no fallback path between environments, in either direction, under any failure.
- Persistence of results into `api_keys.permission_snapshot`, `permission_snapshot_at`, `can_trade`, `can_withdraw`, `can_transfer`, `read_only`, `ip_whitelist`, `ip_whitelist_verified_at`, `status`, `expires_at`, `last_error_code`, `last_error_at`.
- Boot assertion per ADR-0009 item 4: for every key with trading enabled, run the pipeline; any failure puts the app in `Degraded` with order entry disabled and raises a critical alert.
- Scheduled re-check job every 6 h (US-ACCT-003 NFR) with the result cached and timestamped.
- Force-disable behaviour: when a stored key is found to have withdrawal permission, the account is set `trading_enabled = false`, a critical alert is raised and the reason is recorded verbatim for display (US-ACCT-003 scenario 2).

## Out of scope
The admin UI that renders these results (E27-S01, E27-S02); rotation (E27-S03); revocation (E27-S04); the Bybit HTTP client and signing itself (exchange adapter, E08); per-account profiles (E28).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A compliant key is accepted
  Given a candidate key with Withdraw absent, ContractTrade Order and Position present, unified true, a matching UID and an IP whitelist containing the egress IP
  When POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys is called
  Then the response is 201 with verification.passed true and the secret is stored envelope-encrypted, never echoed

Scenario: A key with withdrawal permission is refused
  Given a candidate key whose permissions.Wallet contains "Withdraw"
  When the import is attempted
  Then the response is 422 validation_failed with field api_key, rule key_withdraw_permission and message "permissions.Wallet contains 'Withdraw'", and nothing is persisted

Scenario: A stored key that gains withdrawal permission is force-disabled
  Given a stored, previously compliant key
  When the 6-hourly self-check finds Withdraw present
  Then the account is force-disabled for trading, a critical alert is raised, and the reason is recorded verbatim for display

Scenario: Egress IP not whitelisted
  Given the current egress IP is not in the key's whitelist
  When the self-check runs
  Then the account shows IP mismatch, trading is blocked, and the current egress IP is returned so it can be copied into Bybit

Scenario: Cross-environment key rejected
  Given an account bound to demo
  When a live key is submitted for it
  Then verification fails with "key does not belong to this environment" and nothing is persisted

Scenario: No silent fallback
  Given the demo private WS is unreachable
  When the test endpoint runs with include_ws true
  Then websocket.ok is false with the error text, and no live host is contacted - asserted by a host-selection unit test

Scenario: A failing test is still a 200
  Given a stored key whose WS auth times out
  When POST .../keys/{keyId}/test is called
  Then the response is 200 with passed false, rest.ok true and websocket.ok false

Scenario: Boot assertion degrades the app
  Given a trading-enabled key that fails the pipeline at start-up
  When cv-api starts
  Then the app reports Degraded, order entry is disabled, and a critical alert is raised

Scenario: Clock skew is detected
  Given the host clock is 12 s ahead of Bybit server time
  When the signed probe runs
  Then clock_offset_ms reflects the skew and a warning is attached to the verification result
```

## Technical notes / design
The pipeline is a pure function over an adapter response set, so it is unit-testable against recorded Bybit fixtures without a network. Structure:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VerificationResult:
    passed: bool
    uid: str | None
    unified: bool
    permissions: dict[str, list[str]]
    withdraw_enabled: bool
    ip_whitelist: list[str]
    ip_whitelist_matches_egress: bool
    clock_offset_ms: int | None
    probe_ret_code: int | None
    warnings: list[str]
    failures: list[VerificationFailure]   # rule + message, maps 1:1 to Problem.errors
```

Check ordering matters: the withdrawal check runs before anything is persisted and before any probe, so an over-privileged key is never used for a signed call beyond `query-api`.

Egress-IP determination: the deployment's egress IP comes from configuration (`CV_EGRESS_IP`) with an optional verification lookup; it is never taken from a client-supplied header. ADR-0009 records that Bybit made IP allowlist configuration browser-only in Feb 2026, so the whitelist can only be *read* and compared, never set by CandleViewer - the failure copy must therefore tell the operator what to do in the Bybit dashboard.

Config keys: `CV_EGRESS_IP`, `CV_REQUIRE_IP_WHITELIST` (default true for live), `CV_KEY_SELFCHECK_INTERVAL_S` (default 21600), `CV_KEY_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS` (default 14), `CV_RECV_WINDOW_MS`.

Error codes: `validation_failed` with rules `key_withdraw_permission`, `key_missing_scopes`, `key_uid_mismatch`, `key_not_unified`, `key_ip_whitelist_missing`, `key_ip_whitelist_mismatch`, `key_wrong_environment`, `key_probe_failed`; plus `exchange_unavailable` (502) when Bybit itself is down, which is distinct from a key failure and must not disable the account.

## Test plan
Unit: one test per check, both passing and failing, against recorded `query-api` and `wallet-balance` fixtures; check-ordering test proving the withdrawal check precedes persistence; host-selection test asserting `live` and `demo` never cross; clock-offset computation.
Contract: request and response shapes for `createApiKey` and `testApiKey` validated against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, including the "failed probe is still 200" rule.
Integration: against recorded Bybit fixtures including `retCode` 10003 (invalid key), 10004 (bad signature), 10010 (IP not allowed), 10018 (rate limit) and a 5xx; each maps to a distinct, non-account-disabling outcome except where the spec says otherwise.
Chaos: exchange 5xx and timeout during the 6-hourly job - the previous verification result must remain in force with its timestamp rather than being replaced by a failure.
Coverage >=90%.

## Security notes
This pipeline is the enforcement point for the two most consequential misconfigurations named in ADR-0009: withdrawal enabled and no IP allowlist. STRIDE: **Elevation of privilege** - an over-privileged key reaching storage, prevented by check 2 running before persistence and backstopped by the `ak_no_withdraw` and `ak_snapshot_shape` database constraints; **Spoofing** - a key belonging to another UID, prevented by check 4; **Information disclosure** - verification results must not echo the candidate secret; the `VerificationResult` type holds no credential material and a unit test asserts it; **Denial of service** - an attacker triggering repeated `test` calls to burn the per-UID rate-limit budget, mitigated by a 1-per-minute-per-key server-side throttle on the test endpoint. Data classification: verification results are Confidential (they name UIDs and IP ranges) and are `keys:read`-gated. **Requires the `security` label and Security-engineer review.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A at the API layer. The result rendering, including the rule that "the test result is a list, not a colour" (SCR-126) and that the withdrawal-check result is always shown explicitly (SCR-125), is implemented in E27-S01 and E27-S02.

## Performance notes
The whole import round-trip targets <=3 s (SCR-126 performance note). The `test` endpoint is bounded by the exchange round-trip; it must not hold a request worker while waiting - use the async adapter with a 5 s per-probe timeout and a 12 s overall deadline. The 6-hourly job runs off the request path entirely. Verification must never be executed inline on the order-submit path (budget #4, p95 300 ms).

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_key_verification_total{result,rule}`, `cv_key_verification_seconds`, `cv_key_selfcheck_runs_total{result}`, `cv_keys_failing_policy` (gauge, by rule), `cv_clock_offset_ms` (gauge).
Audit: `account.key_imported` (fingerprint only, never the key), `account.tested`, `account.disabled_by_policy` (the two event names SCR-125 already declares), `security.key_policy_violation {rule, key_id}`.
Alerts: critical on withdrawal-permission detected, on IP mismatch and on boot-assertion failure, routed to the owner's alert channel per US-ACCT-003's NFR "failures page the owner".

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via PR <=400 LOC diff, conventional commits, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner; all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/accounts` and `candleviewer/credentials` (M2 is in the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; no field shipped that is not in the spec, no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: schema/API deltas noted in the PR description; runbook entry added when the change is operational.
- [ ] Observability (metrics, audit events) added and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off (E27-D06 handoff accepted, E27-D07 design QA passed) for any ticket touching UI.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E27-Q05.
- [ ] Secret-leak assertion suite from E27-T02/E27-X02 passes: no key material in logs, traces, metrics, error bodies or support bundles.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-T02** (the broker, because the pipeline must borrow credentials to run the signed probe). Consumes the Bybit REST and private-WS adapter delivered by **E08**, including its `retCode` normalisation and rate-limit handling.

## Branch

title: Add per-account health monitoring, key-age policy evaluation and the wallet snapshot cache
body:
## Context
Three background behaviours are shared by several E27 screens and must exist once, server-side, rather than being re-derived per screen.

US-ACCT-010 requires a per-account connection state with three levels - healthy (private WS connected and authenticated, heartbeat age shown), degraded (WS dropped, REST polling has taken over), and down (neither WS nor REST for 30 s, order entry disabled for that account, dead-man's-switch policy invoked) - with the transition to red happening within 30 s and a heartbeat interval of at most 10 s.

US-ACCT-008 requires a wallet snapshot that is WS-first with a periodic REST truth-check: if the private WS `wallet` stream has been silent for 60 s a REST reconciliation runs; if that also fails the figures are marked stale and risk-based sizing is disabled for that account. The OpenAPI description of `listExchangeAccounts` states the corresponding rule: balances come from the cached wallet snapshot and `balance_stale` is true when the snapshot is older than 10 s.

US-ACCT-005 requires key-age policy evaluation against a configurable policy (default 90 days), with an amber state inside the warning window, a red state when overdue, a daily alert, and the explicit rule that a key is **never** auto-disabled for age alone.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `candleviewer/accounts/health.py`: per-account health state machine with states `healthy`, `degraded`, `down`, driven by private-WS heartbeat age, REST poll success and the last exchange error; transition to `down` within 30 s of the last success; heartbeat expectation <=10 s.
- Publication of health and wallet state on the WS `system` and `wallet` topics per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS13 (`wallet` throttled at 500 ms, `system` at 1000 ms), and exposure through `GET /exchange-accounts` and `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}` as the documented `balance` object with `updated_at` plus the `balance_stale` flag.
- Wallet snapshot cache: WS-first; REST `wallet-balance` reconciliation when the stream has been silent for 60 s; `balance_stale` true when the snapshot is older than 10 s; a `stale_since` timestamp for display; a flag consumed by risk-based sizing so that it is disabled for a stale account.
- Key-age evaluation: `api_keys.rotation_due_at` computed from the creation date recorded at registration (US-ACCT-005 NFR: never from an unverified Bybit expiry field) against the configurable policy; states `ok`, `warn` (inside the window, default 14 days), `overdue`; a daily alert while overdue; never an automatic disable.
- Ordering-enabled gate exposed to the OMS: an account in `down`, force-disabled by policy, stale-for-sizing or lacking an active key must not accept new orders.
- `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate` (operationId `getFeeRate`) served from the same cached-snapshot mechanism.

## Out of scope
The UI rendering of these states (E27-S01, E27-S02, E27-S05); the dead-man's-switch policy itself and the kill-switch (owned by E39); risk caps (E39); the private-WS client (E08); trade-group leg eligibility (E34, which consumes the gate defined here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Healthy account
  Given the private WS is connected and authenticated for an account
  When the account state is read
  Then it is healthy and the last heartbeat age is reported

Scenario: Degraded account
  Given the private WS has dropped and REST polling has taken over
  When the account state is read
  Then it is degraded, and rule actions that require sub-second reaction are flagged in the payload

Scenario: Down within 30 seconds
  Given neither WS nor REST has succeeded for 30 seconds
  When the state machine ticks
  Then the account becomes down within 30 s of the last success, order entry for that account is refused, and the dead-man's-switch policy hook is invoked

Scenario: Wallet reconciliation after silence
  Given the wallet stream has been silent for 60 seconds
  When the reconciliation timer fires
  Then a REST wallet-balance call runs and the freshness timestamp updates

Scenario: Stale balances disable risk-based sizing
  Given both the stream and the reconciliation have failed
  When the account snapshot is served
  Then balance_stale is true, stale_since is populated, and the sizing gate reports risk-based sizing as unavailable for that account

Scenario: Key age warning
  Given a key is 76 days old under a 90-day policy with a 14-day window
  When the policy is evaluated
  Then the key state is warn and an alert is raised once

Scenario: Overdue keys are never auto-disabled
  Given a key exceeds the policy age
  When the policy is evaluated daily
  Then the state is overdue, a daily alert fires, and trading remains enabled

Scenario: Policy change recomputes immediately
  When the policy is changed from 90 to 180 days
  Then every key state is recomputed on the same request, with no wait for the next scheduled run
```

## Technical notes / design
The health state machine is a small explicit FSM with a monotonic clock source, not a set of ad-hoc timestamp comparisons, so that it can be unit-tested with a fake clock and so that a suspended laptop (a real scenario for the WSL deployment) does not produce spurious healthy states.

`balance_stale` has two thresholds which must not be conflated: **10 s** is the display-staleness flag defined by the OpenAPI `listExchangeAccounts` description, while **60 s** is the reconciliation trigger from US-ACCT-008. Both are configurable: `CV_WALLET_STALE_S` (10), `CV_WALLET_RECONCILE_S` (60), `CV_ACCOUNT_DOWN_S` (30), `CV_ACCOUNT_HEARTBEAT_S` (10), `CV_KEY_ROTATION_POLICY_DAYS` (90), `CV_KEY_ROTATION_WARN_DAYS` (14).

The gate exposed to the OMS is a single function `order_entry_allowed(account_id) -> Allowed | Blocked(reason)` so that every consumer - the ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, the rule engine and fan-out - reads the same answer with the same reason string.

## Test plan
Unit: FSM transitions with a fake clock, including suspend-and-resume; stale thresholds at exactly 10 s and 60 s boundaries; key-age states at policy boundaries, including a same-request recompute after a policy change.
Integration: against a fake private-WS that can be dropped and restored, asserting the degraded and down transitions and the reconciliation call.
Contract: the `balance` object and `balance_stale` field shapes against the OpenAPI spec; the `wallet` and `system` WS payloads against `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`.
Chaos: WS kill and restore; REST 5xx during reconciliation; clock jump forwards and backwards by 5 minutes.
Coverage >=90%.

## Security notes
Threat: a **spoofed healthy state** is the dangerous failure here - an account that appears connected while orders cannot actually reach the exchange invites the user to take risk they cannot manage. Mitigation: health is derived from positive evidence (a successful authenticated heartbeat or REST call) and decays on silence; it is never asserted optimistically. Second threat: information disclosure through the health payload - balances and UIDs are Confidential, so every health field is served under `accounts:read` with `scope: granted_accounts`, and the WS `wallet` topic is intersected with the caller's granted account scope (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS13).

## Accessibility notes
State names must be available as text, not colour alone - the payload carries an explicit `state` string plus a human-readable `reason`, which SCR-125 and SCR-079 render as text chips. US-ACCT-010's NFR requires that state transitions are announced to screen readers via a live region; the backend supports that by emitting a discrete transition event rather than only a level, so the client can announce changes rather than poll.

## Performance notes
Health fields refresh on open and every 60 s, never per second (SCR-125 performance note). The `wallet` topic is throttled to 500 ms and `system` to 1000 ms by the protocol. The health evaluation loop must cost <1 ms per account per tick; with at most 6 accounts this is trivial, but the loop must not perform I/O while holding the state lock.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_account_health_state{account,state}` (gauge), `cv_account_health_transitions_total{from,to}`, `cv_wallet_snapshot_age_seconds{account}`, `cv_wallet_reconcile_total{result}`, `cv_keys_rotation_state{state}`.
Audit: `account.health_changed {account_id, from, to, reason}` at INFO; `account.disabled_by_policy` when the gate blocks order entry.
Alerts: key-age warn (once), key-age overdue (daily), account down (immediate).

title: Write the accounts and key-vault operator runbook and amend ADR-0009
body:
## Context
ADR-0009 assigns several operational obligations that only exist as prose today: an owner-held offline KEK backup with a restore runbook stating that "a backup without the KEK is unusable - that is the intended property"; a manual IP-allowlist step in the VPS migration runbook, because Bybit made allowlist configuration browser-only in Feb 2026; and a full rotation drill to be executed once before Live enablement as an R4 PRR item. E27-K01 additionally produces custody decisions that must be written down before the knowledge leaves the person who made them (risk R10, key-person).

This task turns those obligations into runbooks an operator can follow without asking anyone, and records the decisions E27 actually made as an amendment to ADR-0009.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/ops/runbooks/kek-custody.md` finalised from the E27-K01 output: where the KEK lives on the WSL host and on the VPS, how it is injected, how it is backed up offline, how it is rotated, and what happens on loss.
- `docs/ops/runbooks/key-rotation.md`: the operator-side procedure matching the SCR-127 wizard - create the new key in the Bybit dashboard (with the 48 h new-key restriction called out), configure the IP allowlist manually, run the app-side rotation, verify, then delete the old key at Bybit.
- `docs/ops/runbooks/key-compromise.md`: the emergency path - mark compromised, revoke, choose "revoke and leave positions" or "flatten first, then revoke", what to do when the Bybit delete call fails (local deletion is authoritative; revoke manually in the dashboard), and who to notify.
- `docs/ops/runbooks/restore-without-kek.md`: the restore drill, its expected outcome (nothing decrypts, the app refuses trading mode) and how to recover with the offline KEK copy.
- ADR-0009 amendment section recording: the injection mechanism chosen in E27-K01, the config vocabulary, the degraded-mode contract, and the DEK-cache TTL decision from E27-T02.
- A short operator FAQ answering the three questions this design predictably raises: why the secret can never be shown again, why a database backup alone is useless, and why the IP allowlist cannot be set from the app.
- Cross-links added from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` to each runbook.

## Out of scope
Implementation of any of the described mechanisms (E27-K01, T02, T03, S03, S04); the R4 pre-Live rotation drill execution itself (an R4 PRR item, not this ticket); backup tooling (E22).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An operator can rotate a key using only the runbook
  Given an operator who has not worked on E27
  When they follow docs/ops/runbooks/key-rotation.md end to end on the demo environment
  Then the rotation completes with no question asked of the engineering team, and the observation is recorded in the ticket

Scenario: The restore drill produces the intended failure
  Given a database backup restored on a machine without the KEK
  When the runbook's verification steps are followed
  Then no key decrypts, the app refuses trading mode, and the runbook states plainly that this is the intended property rather than a defect

Scenario: The ADR reflects what was built
  When ADR-0009 is read alongside the merged E27 code
  Then the injection mechanism, config keys, degraded contract and DEK-cache TTL described in the amendment match the implementation exactly

Scenario: The manual allowlist step is impossible to miss
  When the VPS migration runbook is reviewed
  Then the manual Bybit IP-allowlist step appears as a blocking checklist item with the consequence of skipping it stated
```

## Technical notes / design
Runbooks follow the existing house format: purpose, preconditions, numbered steps with the exact command or UI action, verification step, rollback, and an escalation contact. Every command is copy-pasteable and every UI action names the screen ID (SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129) so the reader can find it.

The compromise runbook must state the ordering explicitly, because US-ACCT-006's NFR fixes it: **local deletion is authoritative and happens first** - never leave usable material because a remote call failed.

## Test plan
Documentation review rather than automated testing: a second engineer executes each runbook on the demo environment and records the result in the ticket. A CI link-checker validates every relative path. A `docs` test asserts that every runbook referenced from `04-security-program.md` exists.

## Security notes
The runbooks themselves must contain no secret material, no real UIDs and no real IP addresses - placeholders only, with a note saying so. Classification: Internal. The compromise runbook is the response plan for the epic's worst-case threat and is reviewed by the Security engineer as part of E27-X04.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - documentation.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
No code. The runbooks do specify which metrics and audit events an operator should check at each step (`cv_keys_failing_policy`, `cv_account_health_state`, `security.kek_loaded`, `account.key_rotated`), which is what makes them actionable during an incident.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four runbooks and the ADR amendment merged.
- [ ] Each runbook executed once on demo by an engineer who did not write it, with the result recorded.
- [ ] Link-checker green; cross-links added from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- [ ] Reviewed by the Security engineer (also covered by E27-X04) and by DevSecOps.
- [ ] No secret material, real UID or real IP address appears in any runbook.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-T02**, **E27-T03**, **E27-S03** and **E27-S04**, because the runbooks document behaviour that must already exist and have been verified.
