title: Register Bybit main and sub-accounts and browse them on the admin accounts list
body:
## Context
Covers **US-ACCT-001** (register a Bybit account in the app, Must) and **US-ACCT-010** (account health and connection state, Must) as one vertical slice: the `/exchange-accounts` REST surface plus **SCR-125 Admin: Bybit accounts list**, the screen that is the entry point for everything else in this epic and the place where the withdrawal-permission verdict is displayed for every account at once.

SCR-125 is explicit about what the screen must make unmissable: the footer line "Withdrawal permission: OFF on all accounts (verified 14:00)", a per-row state including "IP whitelist missing or mismatched" and "withdrawal permission detected (**critical**, account is auto-disabled for trading with a red banner)", and the rule that "each state is a text chip". US-ACCT-001 adds the sub-account cap: Bybit allows 5 sub-accounts (20 with Business KYC), and adding a sixth must surface the cap and require explicit acknowledgement.

The account shell is registered **without** any key - US-ACCT-001's own NFR says "no secret involved in this story", and the OpenAPI description of `createExchangeAccount` confirms that "API keys are supplied separately". A freshly registered account therefore appears as "no key - inactive".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Backend routes, exactly per `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET /exchange-accounts` (`listExchangeAccounts`, `accounts:read`, scope `granted_accounts`), `POST /exchange-accounts` (`createExchangeAccount`, `accounts:write`, scope `none`), `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}` (`getExchangeAccount`), `PATCH /exchange-accounts/{accountId}` (`updateExchangeAccount` - label, enabled flag, active profile, position/margin mode).
- Registration validation: label unique per environment (`ux_ea_label`), UID unique per exchange and environment (`ux_ea_uid`) with the documented conflict message "This UID is already registered as <label>", `parent_account_id` required for `kind = sub` and forbidden for `kind = main` (`ea_parent_shape`), sub-account env must equal the parent's (`trg_ea_env_parent`).
- Sub-account cap surfacing: when a non-Business-KYC main account already has `max_sub_accounts_hint` (default 5) sub-accounts, registering another returns the cap information and requires an explicit acknowledgement flag on the request; the UI shows the 5 / 20 Business-KYC rule before the acknowledgement.
- **SCR-125** at route `/admin/accounts`, RBAC-gated inside the web app (there is no separate admin application): columns label, UID, environment, permissions, IP allowlist, key age, state; the aggregate withdrawal-permission line with its verification timestamp; empty state; per-row actions (edit, rotate key, disable, delete) that route into their own flows.
- Per-account health chip driven by the E27-T04 state machine and the WS `system` and `wallet` topics: healthy with last heartbeat age, "degraded - REST only", and down with order entry disabled for that account.
- Components used as specified in the catalogue: CMP-001 Button, CMP-011 Tag/Chip, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge, CMP-176 AccountKeyRow.
- The **SCR-019 setup-checklist** item "add a Bybit account" wired to completion, and the **SCR-016** onboarding wizard step 3 reusing the registration form inline (Demo first).
- Audit events `account.created`, `account.updated`, `account.tested`, `account.disabled_by_policy`.

## Out of scope
API-key entry and verification UI (E27-S02); rotation (E27-S03); revoke, disable and delete (E27-S04); balances, leverage and margin mode (E27-S05); per-account profiles (E28); the users-and-roles admin surface (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Add a sub-account
  Given I open Admin - Accounts and choose "Add account"
  When I enter a label, the Bybit UID, the account kind sub and the environment demo, and pick the parent account
  Then the account is created and appears in the list as "no key - inactive"

Scenario: Duplicate UID
  Given an account with UID 10234567 already exists for the live environment
  When I register the same UID for live again
  Then the request fails with conflict and the message "This UID is already registered as Main", and no row is created

Scenario: Sub-account cap surfaced
  Given 5 sub-accounts already exist under a non-Business-KYC main account
  When I attempt to add a sixth
  Then the Bybit cap of 5 regular and 20 with Business KYC is shown and the request is refused until I acknowledge it explicitly

Scenario: Cross-environment parenting refused
  Given a main account bound to live
  When I register a sub-account bound to demo under it
  Then the request is refused before reaching the database, with a message naming the environment mismatch

Scenario: Withdrawal permission is impossible to miss
  Given one account's stored key reports withdrawal permission
  When the accounts list renders
  Then that row shows a blocking error state, the account is shown as auto-disabled for trading, the aggregate footer line no longer claims withdrawal is OFF on all accounts, and the verdict is text, not colour alone

Scenario: Health states are text
  Given one account is healthy, one degraded and one down
  When the list renders
  Then each state is a text chip naming the state and its reason, the healthy row shows the last heartbeat age, and the down row shows that order entry is disabled

Scenario: Manager scope
  Given a manager granted access to exactly one account
  When they open the accounts list
  Then only that account is returned, and requesting another account's detail returns 403 with an audit row and no state change

Scenario: Health chip updates without a reload
  Given the list is open and an account's private WS drops
  When the system topic publishes the transition
  Then the row moves to degraded within one throttle window and the change is announced to screen readers via a live region
```

## Technical notes / design
RBAC is enforced server-side only: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` note C5 states "the client is never trusted for account scope" and the scope is re-derived from the token on every call. The list route therefore filters by `user_account_access`, and the UI's hiding of rows is cosmetic, never the control.

`GET /exchange-accounts` serves balances from the cached wallet snapshot maintained by the private-WS `wallet` stream, with `balance_stale` true when the snapshot is older than 10 s - both behaviours come from E27-T04, not from this story.

The registration form is shared code between SCR-125's "Add account" modal and SCR-016 onboarding step 3; it is built as one component with a `variant` prop rather than duplicated.

Error codes: `conflict` (duplicate UID or label), `validation_failed` (bad shape, parent rules, cap not acknowledged), `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`.

## Test plan
Unit (backend): validation matrix for kind/parent/env combinations; cap acknowledgement logic; conflict message formatting.
Unit (frontend): table rendering per state; cap dialog; empty state; form validation.
Contract: `listExchangeAccounts`, `createExchangeAccount`, `getExchangeAccount`, `updateExchangeAccount` against the OpenAPI document.
Integration: registration through to a row in `exchange_accounts` with the correct audit row.
E2E (Playwright, added in E27-Q02): register a demo sub-account, see it as "no key - inactive", then see its health chip change when the fake WS drops.
A11y: axe-core clean on SCR-125; manual screen-reader pass on the state chips and the live region.
Coverage >=90% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: **Elevation of privilege** - a manager enumerating accounts they were not granted; mitigated by server-side scope derivation and asserted by the RBAC matrix test in E27-X03. **Information disclosure** - UIDs are Confidential and must not appear in client-side analytics events. **Tampering** - `PATCH` must not be able to change `env`, `exchange_uid` or `kind`; those are immutable after creation and the route rejects attempts with `validation_failed`. Every state-changing control is wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger so an audit row cannot be forgotten. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-125's own rules apply: every state is a text chip and the withdrawal-check result is always shown explicitly, never by colour alone. The table follows CMP-049's keyboard semantics - arrow-key cell navigation, a visible focus ring at >=3:1 contrast, and row actions reachable in tab order. Health transitions are announced through an `aria-live="polite"` region (US-ACCT-010 NFR: "states announced to screen readers via a live region"); the down state, which disables order entry, is announced assertively. The cap dialog is a `role="dialog"` with the cap stated in text. Contrast >=4.5:1 for text and >=3:1 for the chip borders in both themes; the layout survives 125% zoom and 200% text scaling.

## Performance notes
The account list is at most 6 rows in v1, so rendering cost is irrelevant; what matters is the refresh discipline from SCR-125: health fields refresh on open and every 60 s, never per second. The initial list render must complete within 300 ms of the API response. WS-driven chip updates are coalesced by the protocol's `wallet` (500 ms) and `system` (1000 ms) throttles.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_admin_accounts_list_seconds`, `cv_accounts_registered_total{kind,env}`.
Audit: `account.created` (payload records the UID and label, never a key), `account.updated` (before and after), `account.tested`, `account.disabled_by_policy`.
Analytics: `admin.accounts_list_viewed`.
Frontend error boundary reports render failures with the screen ID SCR-125.

title: Add and edit a Bybit account's API key with write-only fields and a mandatory connection test
body:
## Context
Covers **US-ACCT-002** (store an API key with envelope encryption, Must), **US-ACCT-003** (API key self-check, Must) and **US-ACCT-007** (environment binding per account, Must) on the UI side, through **SCR-126 Admin: add / edit Bybit account**.

SCR-126 fixes the interaction precisely: the API key and secret are **write-only fields, never rendered back**, a mandatory connection test must pass before saving, withdrawal permission present is a **hard block**, and the test result is rendered as a list rather than a colour. Edit mode leaves the secret field empty and optional. Save is gated behind step-up authentication, and the audit payload records a key **fingerprint only**.

US-ACCT-002's second scenario is the durable constraint for the whole codebase: "the secret field shows a masked placeholder and there is no reveal control anywhere in the app or API". The third scenario - KEK unavailable - surfaces here as the blocking banner that puts the app in read-only mode.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-126** as a modal reachable from SCR-125 and inline as onboarding step 3 (SCR-016): label, environment radio (Demo / Live), API key and secret as `type=password` write-only fields, IP whitelist display, intended-permissions checklist, a "Test connection" action and a step-up-gated Save.
- Wiring to `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys` and `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}/test` from E27-T03, rendering the full `verification` object as a list of checks: read ok, trade ok, withdrawal DISABLED ok, UID, unified, IP allowlist and egress match, clock offset, probe return code, warnings.
- Failure rendering with actionable copy for every documented rule: `key_withdraw_permission` (hard block, save disabled), `key_missing_scopes`, `key_uid_mismatch`, `key_not_unified`, `key_ip_whitelist_missing`, `key_ip_whitelist_mismatch` (showing the current egress IP for copy-paste into Bybit, per US-ACCT-003 scenario 3), `key_wrong_environment` (US-ACCT-007 scenario 2), `key_probe_failed`.
- The Bybit 48-hour new-key restriction stated inline, as SCR-126's wireframe shows.
- Edit mode: secret optional and empty; leaving it blank changes metadata only and does not touch ciphertext.
- Masked display everywhere else in the app via CMP-034 MaskedValue, showing `...{key_id_last4}` only; **no reveal affordance exists in any component, screen or API**.
- The degraded banner for US-ACCT-002 scenario 3: when the backend reports the KEK is unavailable, a blocking CMP-028 banner appears, the app is read-only, and every trading control is disabled with an explanatory message.
- Components: CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError, CMP-034 MaskedValue, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge.
- Audit `account.created` / `account.updated` with the key **fingerprint only**, emitted through CMP-093.

## Out of scope
The verification pipeline itself (E27-T03); the credential broker (E27-T02); rotation (E27-S03); revocation (E27-S04); the key health panel SCR-128 (E27-S03); step-up authentication implementation (E09, consumed here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Key stored with envelope encryption
  Given I paste an API key and secret for a demo account and the connection test passes
  When I save with step-up authentication
  Then the secret is stored encrypted under a per-record DEK wrapped by the KEK, only the key-id tail is retained in clear, and the response contains no secret material

Scenario: The secret is never re-displayed
  Given a saved key
  When I reopen the key record anywhere in the app
  Then the secret field shows a masked placeholder, there is no reveal control, and no API response contains the secret

Scenario: Withdrawal permission is a hard block
  Given the pasted key has withdrawal permission enabled
  When the connection test runs
  Then the result list shows the withdrawal check as failed with the verbatim reason, Save stays disabled, and nothing is persisted

Scenario: Egress IP not whitelisted
  Given the deployment egress IP is not in the key's Bybit allowlist
  When the test runs
  Then the failure names the check, displays the current egress IP for copy-paste into Bybit, and explains that the allowlist must be set in the Bybit dashboard because it cannot be configured from here

Scenario: Cross-environment key rejected
  Given the account is bound to demo
  When I paste a live key
  Then the test fails with "key does not belong to this environment" and Save is refused

Scenario: Save requires a passing test
  Given the connection test has not been run or did not pass
  When I attempt to save
  Then Save is disabled and the reason is stated in text next to the button

Scenario: Edit without changing the secret
  Given an existing key
  When I change only the label and save
  Then the ciphertext, nonce and dek_ref are unchanged and the audit row records a metadata-only update

Scenario: KEK unavailable
  Given the backend reports that the KEK cannot be loaded
  When any screen renders
  Then a blocking banner is shown, the app is read-only, and all trading controls are disabled with the reason stated

Scenario: Nothing is echoed on failure
  Given a rejected key
  When the error response and the browser console, network tab and any client-side log are inspected
  Then the submitted secret appears in none of them
```

## Technical notes / design
The form posts to the backend and never talks to Bybit from the browser - SCR-128 states the panel "never calls the exchange directly from the browser", and the same holds here. The plaintext exists in the browser only inside the controlled input value and in the request body over TLS on the Tailscale-only network; the field is cleared from component state as soon as the response arrives, on unmount and on navigation away.

Autocomplete is disabled on both credential fields (`autocomplete="off"`, `spellcheck="false"`, `data-1p-ignore`) so that password managers and browser autofill do not capture the material. The fields are `type=password` with an explicit description that the value is write-only.

The verification result renders from the `VerificationResult` shape defined in E27-T03; the UI must not re-derive pass or fail from individual fields, so that the backend stays the single source of the verdict.

Step-up: Save calls `POST /auth/step-up` first (E09) and attaches the resulting elevated-session assertion; a failed or expired step-up blocks the save without losing the form contents apart from the credential fields, which are always cleared.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): field write-only behaviour; result-list rendering per failure rule; Save enablement matrix; state clearing on unmount, navigation and response; a test asserting the secret value never reaches any store, console or analytics payload.
Contract: `createApiKey` and `testApiKey` request and response shapes, including the 422 `key_withdraw_permission` example from the OpenAPI document and the "failed probe is still 200" rule.
Integration: full import against recorded Bybit fixtures for each failure rule.
E2E (E27-Q02): import a compliant demo key end to end; attempt a withdrawal-enabled key and assert the hard block.
Security test: a browser-level assertion that the submitted secret is absent from `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, the console and any outbound analytics request.
A11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass on the write-only description and the result list.
Coverage >=80% frontend, >=90% backend paths touched.

## Security notes
This screen is where key material enters the system, so it carries the epic's tightest controls. Threats: **Information disclosure** - autofill capture, client-side logging, an error body echoing the submitted value, a screenshot in a support bundle; mitigated by write-only fields, autocomplete suppression, state clearing and the no-echo assertions above. **Elevation of privilege** - saving an over-privileged key; structurally impossible because the backend refuses to persist it (E27-T03) and the database refuses it (`ak_no_withdraw`). **Repudiation** - mitigated by step-up plus the CMP-093 audit wrapper, with the audit payload carrying a fingerprint only. Data classification: Secret in transit, never at rest on the client. **Requires the `security` label and Security-engineer review before merge.**

## Accessibility notes
Secret fields are `type=password` with an explicit programmatic description stating that the value is write-only and will never be shown again (SCR-126: "secret fields are `type=password` with an explicit 'value is write-only' description"). The test result is a list of labelled statements, not a colour - each check renders as "Withdrawal permission: off - pass" style text. Failure messages are associated with their field through `aria-describedby` and announced via `aria-live="assertive"`. The modal traps focus, opens focus on the first field, and returns focus to the invoking control on close. Contrast >=4.5:1 in both themes; full keyboard operability including the step-up dialog; the blocking KEK banner is `role="alert"`.

## Performance notes
SCR-126 sets the budget: the backend performs live credential validation against Bybit before persisting, the form shows a validating state, and the whole round-trip targets <=3 s. The UI must show progressive per-check results rather than a single spinner where the backend streams them, and must not block the main thread while waiting. The test action is throttled to once per minute per key to protect the per-UID rate-limit budget.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_key_import_attempts_total{result,rule}`, `cv_key_import_seconds`, `cv_key_test_total{result}`.
Audit: `account.created`, `account.updated` (step-up recorded, fingerprint only), `account.tested`, `security.key_policy_violation`.
Analytics: `admin.key_form_opened`, `admin.key_test_run` - neither carries any key-derived value beyond `key_id_last4`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via PR <=400 LOC diff, conventional commits, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner; all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/accounts` and `candleviewer/credentials` (M2 is in the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; no field shipped that is not in the spec, no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: schema/API deltas noted in the PR description; runbook entry added when the change is operational.
- [ ] Observability (metrics, audit events) added and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off (E27-D06 handoff accepted, E27-D07 design QA passed) for any ticket touching UI.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E27-Q05.
- [ ] Secret-leak assertion suite from E27-T02/E27-X02 passes: no key material in logs, traces, metrics, error bodies or support bundles.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-T03** (the verification pipeline and both routes), **E27-S01** (the accounts list this modal is launched from) and **E27-D06** (signed-off handoff). Consumes step-up authentication from **E09**.

## Branch
`feat/e27-key-import-ui` - two PRs: (1) the form and write-only field behaviour, (2) the verification result list, failure copy and the degraded banner.

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#2-acct--bybit-accounts--api-keys` - US-ACCT-001..010 with their Gherkin and NFRs

title: Rotate an API key with an overlap window and surface key-age policy in the health panel
body:
## Context
Covers **US-ACCT-004** (key rotation with overlap, Should) and **US-ACCT-005** (key rotation policy reminder, Should), delivered through **SCR-127 Admin: API key rotation** and **SCR-128 Admin: key health & secrets policy panel**.

The behaviour is fixed by three documents that agree with each other. US-ACCT-004: new requests use the new key while the old key stays valid for a drain window; rotation must not cancel open orders; step-up TOTP is required; every step is audited; if the replacement fails the self-check, promotion is refused and the old key stays primary. The OpenAPI `rotateApiKey` description: two-phase rotation through the same verification pipeline as import, `overlap_seconds` default 300, private WS re-authenticated with the new key at the start of the overlap, and the rotation recorded in `api_key_rotations`. The schema document: new key imported as `pending`, validated with a signed `wallet-balance` call, old key set `rotating` and new `active`, old key revoked after the grace window **with zero in-flight orders**.

Note the one discrepancy to resolve in implementation: the user story says a 15-minute drain window while the API default is `overlap_seconds: 300`. The API default governs (it is the contract); the window is configurable up to 15 minutes, and the UI shows the live countdown either way.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-127** as a stepper wizard: create the new key on Bybit (with an instruction checklist and the 48-hour restriction implication), enter it, test it, switch traffic, verify, revoke the old key - with rollback available until the old key is revoked.
- Wiring to `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}/rotate` (`rotateApiKey`, `keys:manage`, `x-idempotency: required`), rendering the returned `ApiKeyRotation` (`rotation_id`, `old_key_id`, `new_key`, `verification`, `overlap_until`, `state`).
- Drain semantics implemented server-side: during the overlap both keys authenticate; new requests use the new key; the old key is revoked only when the overlap expires **and** there are no in-flight orders; open orders are never cancelled by rotation.
- Private-WS re-authentication with the new key at the start of the overlap, without dropping subscriptions where the protocol allows.
- Refusal path: a replacement key that fails the E27-T03 pipeline does not get promoted, the old key remains primary, and the failure reason is displayed verbatim.
- **SCR-128** key health and secrets policy panel inside `/admin/accounts`: per-key age against policy, last successful use, failure counts, per-UID rate-limit consumption, envelope-encryption status (KEK id and last re-wrap), the configurable rotation policy, and the plain statement that secrets are never displayed, exported or logged.
- Key-age chips from E27-T04: amber "rotate within 14 days" inside the window, red when overdue with a daily alert, and never an automatic disable for age alone; changing the policy recomputes every warning immediately.
- "Mark as compromised" emergency action with its stated immediate effect (key disabled, orders halted for that account), routing into the revoke flow of E27-S04.
- Components: CMP-027, CMP-028, CMP-033 CopyButton, CMP-034 MaskedValue, CMP-035 Countdown, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-049 Table, CMP-066 Stepper, CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-175, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile.

## Out of scope
Revoke, disable and delete flows (E27-S04, invoked from here); KEK rotation and the DEK re-wrap job (E27-T02, whose status this panel merely displays); the verification pipeline (E27-T03); scheduled or unattended rotation (explicitly manual in v1).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overlapping rotation
  Given an account with an active key
  When I add a replacement key, it passes verification, and I mark it primary with step-up authentication
  Then new requests use the new key while the old key remains valid until overlap_until, and the rotation row is written to api_key_rotations

Scenario: Rotation never cancels open orders
  Given the account has three open orders
  When a rotation completes
  Then all three orders are still open and unmodified, asserted against the OMS order list before and after

Scenario: Old key revoked at the end of the window
  When the overlap window ends with no in-flight orders, or I revoke early
  Then the old key is deleted from local storage, a Bybit revoke is attempted, and the outcome of that attempt is displayed

Scenario: Drain waits for in-flight orders
  Given an order is in flight when the overlap expires
  When the revoke step runs
  Then it waits for the in-flight order to settle before revoking, and the UI shows that it is waiting and why

Scenario: New key fails the self-check
  Given the replacement key has withdrawal permission or fails any other check
  When promotion is attempted
  Then promotion is refused, the old key remains primary and active, and the failure reason is displayed verbatim

Scenario: Rollback before revocation
  Given the rotation is at the "switch traffic" step and I choose to roll back
  When the rollback executes
  Then the old key returns to active, the new key is discarded, and both states are audited

Scenario: Warning window
  Given a key is 76 days old under a 90-day policy
  When the accounts screen renders
  Then an amber "rotate within 14 days" chip appears and an alert has been raised

Scenario: Overdue never auto-disables
  Given a key exceeds the policy age
  Then the chip is red, a daily alert fires, and trading for that account continues

Scenario: Policy change recomputes immediately
  When I change the rotation policy from 90 to 180 days
  Then every key's warning state recomputes on the same request, with no scheduled-job delay
```

## Technical notes / design
Rotation is a server-side state machine persisted in `api_key_rotations`, not a UI sequence - so a browser crash mid-rotation cannot leave the system in an ambiguous state. States: `verifying` -> `overlapping` -> `draining` -> `completed`, with `rolled_back` and `failed` as terminals. The wizard reads the state, it does not own it.

The "zero in-flight orders" precondition is read from the OMS (E29). If E29's in-flight query is unavailable, revocation waits and surfaces that it is waiting rather than proceeding blind - failing safe means keeping a valid key slightly longer, never revoking under uncertainty.

Because `ux_api_keys_active` permits exactly one `active` key per account, the overlap is represented as old key `rotating` plus new key `active`, which is exactly why the schema defines the `rotating` status. Any implementation that tries to hold two `active` rows will be rejected by the database.

Config keys: `CV_KEY_ROTATION_OVERLAP_S` (default 300, maximum 900), `CV_KEY_ROTATION_POLICY_DAYS` (default 90), `CV_KEY_ROTATION_WARN_DAYS` (default 14).

## Test plan
Unit: rotation state machine transitions including rollback and failure; overlap countdown; policy-state computation at boundaries; the "waiting for in-flight orders" branch.
Integration: full rotation against recorded Bybit fixtures with a fake OMS reporting in-flight orders; assert open orders are untouched before and after.
Contract: `rotateApiKey` request and response against the OpenAPI document.
Chaos: backend restart mid-overlap - the state machine resumes from `api_key_rotations` and neither key is lost; WS drop during re-authentication.
E2E (E27-Q02): rotate a demo key through the wizard, including the failed-replacement refusal path.
A11y: axe-core on SCR-127 and SCR-128; manual screen-reader pass on the stepper.
Coverage >=90% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: **Denial of service through self-inflicted lockout** - the primary risk of rotation is losing trading access mid-position; mitigated by verify-before-promote, the overlap window, rollback until revocation, and the refusal to revoke while orders are in flight. **Information disclosure** - the new secret is entered here and is subject to every control from E27-S02 (write-only, no echo, cleared from state). **Repudiation** - step-up TOTP is required and every step is audited, per US-ACCT-004's NFR. **Tampering** - the rotation is idempotent (`x-idempotency: required`), so a replayed request cannot start a second rotation. SCR-127's audit rule applies: `account.key_rotated` at high severity with fingerprints only. Data classification: Secret in transit. **Requires the `security` label and Security-engineer review.**

## Accessibility notes
SCR-127's rules: the wizard is a stepper dialog where each step is a labelled region with `aria-current="step"`, and the secret field is write-only with a label that says so. SCR-128 renders as a table of keys plus a policy section written in plain sentences, with warnings as text plus an icon, never colour alone. The overlap countdown (CMP-035) is announced at meaningful intervals rather than every second, and its remaining time is available as text to assistive technology. Rollback and revoke are `role="alertdialog"` confirmations naming the consequence. Full keyboard operability; focus returns to the launching row on close.

## Performance notes
SCR-127 sets a <=10 s target for the whole rotation, with each stage and its elapsed time shown. The overlap is 300 s by default and is not part of that budget. SCR-128 computes health server-side and caches it for 60 s, and never calls the exchange directly from the browser. The rate-limit consumption display reads the governor's published budget rather than probing.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_key_rotations_total{result}`, `cv_key_rotation_seconds`, `cv_key_rotation_state` (gauge by state), `cv_keys_rotation_state{state}` reused from E27-T04.
Audit: `account.key_rotated` (high severity, fingerprints only), `admin.secrets_policy_changed {key, before, after}` and `admin.key_marked_compromised` (both high severity, as SCR-128 declares), `admin.key_health_viewed` (analytics only).
Alerts: rotation failure, rotation stuck in `draining` beyond twice the overlap window, key overdue (daily).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via PR <=400 LOC diff, conventional commits, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner; all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/accounts` and `candleviewer/credentials` (M2 is in the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.

- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E27-Q05.
- [ ] Secret-leak assertion suite from E27-T02/E27-X02 passes: no key material in logs, traces, metrics, error bodies or support bundles.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-T03** (the replacement key runs the same verification pipeline), **E27-T04** (key-age policy states and health), **E27-S02** (the credential entry form this wizard reuses) and **E27-D06** (signed-off handoff). Reads in-flight order state from **E29** (OMS core); if that interface is not yet available the drain step fails safe by waiting.

title: Revoke a key immediately and disable or delete an account with consequences stated up front
body:
## Context
Covers **US-ACCT-006** (revoke a key immediately, Must) through **SCR-129 Admin: account disable / delete confirmation** and the revoke action on SCR-125 and SCR-127.

US-ACCT-006 exists so that a suspected compromise can be answered in seconds, and its NFR is the design rule for the whole flow: **local deletion is authoritative** - never leave usable material because a remote call failed. The three scenarios are exact: revoke with step-up deletes the key locally, attempts a Bybit delete, makes the account inactive and disarms all its rules; if open positions exist the operator must choose "revoke and leave positions" or "flatten first, then revoke"; and if the Bybit delete errors, local deletion still happens, the failure is displayed with the exact error, and the operator is instructed to revoke in the Bybit dashboard.

SCR-129 adds the account-level flows and is explicit that disable and delete are **separate flows with different copy**, that open positions are not closed automatically, that assigned users lose access, and that rules scoped to the account are disarmed and listed by name.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Revoke action wired to `DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}` (`revokeApiKey`, `keys:manage`, `x-idempotency: optional`), which the OpenAPI describes as local revocation that drops the account to `key_status: missing` and halts its private streams.
- Local-first ordering: destroy the credential through the E27-T02 broker and set `revoked_at`, **then** attempt the Bybit-side delete; a failure of the remote call is reported with its exact error and never rolls back the local deletion.
- Consequence summary fetched before the dialog renders (SCR-129: the confirm button does not appear until the summary has loaded, target <=1 s): open positions with counts, working orders, running emulated algos, assigned users, and rules scoped to the account listed **by name**.
- Open-position branch: "revoke and leave positions" or "flatten first, then revoke", the latter delegating to the flatten path owned by E29/E39 and waiting for its completion before revoking.
- Rule disarm: every rule bound to the account is disarmed as part of revocation and the list of disarmed rules is shown.
- WS consequences per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS9: affected subscriptions are terminated with `revoked` carrying reason `key_revoked` or `account_disabled` - never silently emptied, "which would look like a flat book or a closed position".
- **SCR-129** disable and delete flows: typed account label plus step-up; distinct copy per flow; deletion refused while open positions, working orders or running algos exist, each listed with counts; the statement that historical records are retained; `DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}` (`deleteExchangeAccount`) performing a soft deactivation that sets `deleted_at`.
- Components: CMP-027, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- Audit `account.disabled`, `account.deleted`, `account.key_revoked`.

## Out of scope
The flatten-all implementation (E29 and E39, invoked here); rule-engine internals (E35, whose disarm interface is consumed); user-access revocation UI (E42); the key rotation wizard (E27-S03, which links into this flow).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Revoke
  Given I select an account's key and confirm revoke with step-up authentication
  Then the key is deleted from local storage first, a Bybit delete is attempted, the account becomes inactive, all rules scoped to it are disarmed and listed, and its private streams are halted

Scenario: Open positions present
  Given the account has two open positions
  When I trigger revoke
  Then the position list is shown and I must choose "revoke and leave positions" or "flatten first, then revoke" before the action proceeds

Scenario: Bybit delete fails
  Given the Bybit revoke call returns an error
  When revocation runs
  Then local deletion has already happened and is not rolled back, the exact exchange error is displayed, and I am instructed to revoke the key in the Bybit dashboard

Scenario: Subscriptions are revoked explicitly
  Given a client is subscribed to orders, positions and wallet for the account
  When the key is revoked
  Then those subscriptions are terminated with a revoked frame carrying reason key_revoked, and are never silently emptied

Scenario: Delete refused while exposure exists
  Given the account has an open position
  When I attempt to delete the account
  Then deletion is refused, the open positions, working orders and running algos are listed with counts, and a "flatten first" shortcut is offered

Scenario: Disable and delete are different
  When I open the disable flow and then the delete flow
  Then the copy, the consequences listed and the confirmation requirements differ, and delete states plainly that it is irreversible

Scenario: Typed confirmation and step-up
  Given the delete dialog is open
  When I type the wrong account label
  Then the confirm control stays disabled; and when the label is correct, step-up authentication is still required before the action runs

Scenario: Historical records survive
  Given an account is deleted
  When the journal and audit log are queried
  Then its historical executions, journal entries and audit rows are still present and the account is soft-deleted with deleted_at set
```

## Technical notes / design
Ordering is the whole design: `broker.destroy(key_id)` and the local `revoked_at` write commit **before** any exchange call is attempted, in one transaction, so that a crash between the two leaves the safe state (no usable local material) rather than the unsafe one.

The consequence summary is a single server-side aggregate query (positions, orders, algos, grants, rules) returned as one object, so the dialog cannot render a partial picture. SCR-129 requires the confirm button to be withheld until it has loaded.

Idempotency: revoke is safe to repeat; a second call on an already-revoked key returns 204 and writes no second audit row beyond a de-duplicated note.

Rule disarm uses the rule engine's disarm interface (E35) scoped by `rule_scope = 'account'`; the returned names populate the dialog. If the rule engine is unavailable, revocation still proceeds - credential destruction must never be blocked by a downstream dependency - and the failure to disarm is raised as a critical alert so it is handled manually.

## Test plan
Unit: ordering test asserting local destruction commits before the exchange call, including a fault injected between the two; consequence-summary aggregation; typed-confirmation and step-up gating.
Integration: revoke with the Bybit delete stubbed to fail - assert local deletion persisted and the exact error surfaced; revoke with open positions through both branches.
Contract: `revokeApiKey` and `deleteExchangeAccount`; the WS `revoked` frame shape and its reason values.
Chaos: process kill between local deletion and the exchange call; restart must show the key gone locally and surface the un-attempted remote revoke as an outstanding manual action.
E2E (E27-Q02): revoke a demo key with an open position through the "flatten first" branch.
A11y: axe-core on SCR-129; manual screen-reader pass on the alertdialog.
Coverage >=90% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
This is the incident-response control for the epic's worst case. Threats: **Denial of service through mis-clicks** - mitigated by typed confirmation plus step-up; **Elevation of privilege** - revoke and delete require `keys:manage` and `accounts:write` with scope `none` (owner-only), asserted by the E27-X03 matrix; **Repudiation** - every step audited with the actor and the chosen branch; **Information disclosure** - the consequence summary names positions and users, so it is served under the same scope rules as the rest of the epic. The dangerous anti-pattern this ticket exists to prevent is rolling back local deletion when a remote call fails, which would leave usable credentials behind after the operator believes they are gone. Data classification: Confidential. **Requires the `security` label and Security-engineer review.**

## Accessibility notes
SCR-129's rules apply: the dialog is `role="alertdialog"` restating the consequences as a list (open positions, working orders, running algos, assigned users, historical records), the account label must be typed to confirm, and **focus starts on Cancel**, not on the destructive action. The exchange error text is announced via `aria-live="assertive"`. The branch choice for open positions is a radio group with the consequence of each option written out, not an icon. Full keyboard operability; the confirm control is disabled - and programmatically marked as such - until both the typed label and the loaded summary conditions are met. Contrast >=4.5:1 including the danger styling.

## Performance notes
The consequence summary must load in <=1 s (SCR-129) and the dialog must not render a confirm control before it does. Local revocation itself is a single transaction and must complete in <=100 ms; the exchange call is attempted asynchronously with a 5 s timeout and its result is streamed into the dialog, so a slow exchange never delays the safe local outcome.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_key_revocations_total{result,remote_result}`, `cv_account_disabled_total{reason}`, `cv_account_deleted_total`.
Audit: `account.key_revoked` (high severity, actor, branch chosen, remote result), `account.disabled`, `account.deleted`, `security.credential_destroyed` from the broker.
Alerts: critical when the remote revoke fails (the operator must act in the Bybit dashboard); critical when rule disarm fails.

## Dependencies

Consumes the flatten path from **E29**/**E39** and the rule-disarm interface from **E35**; both are invoked defensively so that credential destruction is never blocked by their availability.

## Branch

title: Show per-account balance, margin and connection state and control leverage and margin mode
body:
## Context
Covers **US-ACCT-008** (account balance and margin snapshot, Must), **US-ACCT-009** (leverage and margin mode control, Must) and the trading-side rendering of **US-ACCT-010** (account health), through **SCR-079 Account detail drawer (trading-side)** - the surface a trader opens from the account picker or the positions grid.

Two rules dominate. US-ACCT-008's NFR: WS-first with a periodic REST truth-check, and **never show a number without a freshness indicator**; when reconciliation also fails the figures grey out with a "stale since <time>" badge and risk-based sizing is disabled for that account. US-ACCT-009: leverage and margin-mode changes are applied through Bybit and reflected in the snapshot; an open position that blocks the change surfaces the exact exchange reason and restores the previous UI value; and a request exceeding the account profile's leverage cap is refused **client- and server-side before any exchange call**.

SCR-079 adds that no secret material is ever rendered here and that key identifiers are shown truncated.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-079** drawer opened from the account picker (CMP-105) and the positions grid: equity, wallet balance, available balance, used margin, unrealised PnL, margin mode, position mode, leverage, today's realised PnL, fees paid, funding paid and received, a profile-limits summary, key status (valid / expiring / restricted) and, for owners, quick links into SCR-125 and SCR-131.
- Freshness indicator on every figure, sourced from the E27-T04 wallet snapshot: `updated_at`, the `balance_stale` flag at the 10 s threshold, and the `stale_since` badge when both the stream and the REST reconciliation have failed.
- Health banner states from SCR-079: healthy, key expiring soon, key invalid ("This account's API key was rejected - trading disabled for it") and IP-whitelist mismatch with explicit remediation text.
- Leverage control (CMP-104 LeverageSlider) wired to `PATCH /positions/{positionId}/leverage` (`setPositionLeverage`, `positions:write`, scope `granted_accounts`), with risk-limit tiers from the instrument data shown alongside the choice (US-ACCT-009 NFR).
- Margin-mode and position-mode controls (CMP-128 MarginModeToggle, CMP-129 PositionModeToggle) wired to `PATCH /exchange-accounts/{accountId}` (`updateExchangeAccount`, which the OpenAPI defines as updating label, enabled flag, active profile and position/margin mode).
- Profile-cap enforcement: a requested leverage above the account profile's cap is refused in the client **and** by the server before any exchange call, with the message "Your profile caps leverage at 10x" (the exact copy used by SCR-060).
- Blocked-by-open-position handling: the exact exchange reason is surfaced and the previous value is restored in the UI.
- `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate` (`getFeeRate`) rendered in the fees row.
- Subscription to the WS `wallet` topic scoped to the account, per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS13 (500 ms throttle, snapshot plus whole-object last-write-wins).
- Components: CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-104, CMP-106 ProfileBadge, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-128, CMP-129, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge.

## Out of scope
The order ticket and its sizing logic (E30); per-account profile CRUD, which owns the caps this screen enforces (E28); positions and orders blotters (E29); paper-balance reset (E38); risk caps and lockouts (E39).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Snapshot displayed with freshness
  Given an account is verified and connected
  When the drawer opens
  Then equity, available balance, used margin, margin mode and position mode are shown, each with a freshness timestamp, and no figure is rendered without one

Scenario: Reconciliation after silence
  Given the wallet stream has been silent for 60 seconds
  When reconciliation runs
  Then a REST wallet-balance call updates the figures and the freshness timestamp

Scenario: Stale data disables risk-based sizing
  Given the stream is silent and reconciliation has also failed
  When the drawer renders
  Then the figures are greyed with a "stale since <time>" badge and risk-based sizing is reported as unavailable for that account

Scenario: Set leverage
  Given I choose 10x for BTCUSDT on account A and the profile permits it
  When I apply
  Then the change is sent to Bybit and the new value is reflected in the account snapshot

Scenario: Blocked by an open position
  Given an open position prevents the leverage change
  When the exchange rejects it
  Then the exact exchange reason is displayed and the previous value is restored in the UI

Scenario: Exceeds the profile cap
  Given the account profile caps leverage at 10x
  When I request 20x
  Then the request is refused in the client and, if forced, by the server, in both cases before any exchange call is made

Scenario: Key invalid banner
  Given the account's key has been rejected
  When the drawer opens
  Then the banner reads "This account's API key was rejected - trading disabled for it" and trading controls in the drawer are disabled

Scenario: No secret is rendered
  When every field of the drawer is inspected, including the key status row
  Then no secret material appears and the key identifier is shown truncated
```

## Technical notes / design
Freshness is a first-class field, not a decoration: the view model pairs every numeric with `{value, updated_at, stale}` so that it is structurally impossible to render a number without its freshness. A lint rule or a typed wrapper (`Fresh<T>`) is the mechanism; a bare number in the template fails review.

Profile caps are read from the account profile (E28). Until E28 lands, the client reads the cap from the account payload's profile summary and the server enforces from the same source - the enforcement point is the server, and the client check exists only to give a fast, clear message.

Leverage changes are per-symbol (US-ACCT-009 speaks of "per-symbol leverage"), so the control is bound to the drawer's current symbol context and states which symbol it will affect.

The drawer opens from cached state in <=100 ms and refreshes in place (SCR-079 performance note), so it must not block on a network call to render.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): freshness rendering, including the greyed-and-stale state; cap refusal; previous-value restoration after an exchange rejection; the `Fresh<T>` wrapper preventing a bare render.
Unit (backend): server-side cap enforcement before any adapter call, asserted by a test that fails if an exchange call is made.
Contract: `setPositionLeverage`, `updateExchangeAccount`, `getFeeRate`, and the `wallet` WS payload.
Integration: against recorded Bybit fixtures for a leverage change blocked by an open position, and for a successful change.
E2E (E27-Q02): open the drawer on demo, change leverage within the cap, then attempt to exceed it.
A11y: axe-core; manual screen-reader pass on the description list and the toggles.
Coverage >=90% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: **Information disclosure** - balances, UIDs and fee rates are Confidential and the drawer is served under `accounts:read` with `scope: granted_accounts`; a manager must never see another manager's account, which the E27-X03 matrix asserts. **Tampering** - client-side cap enforcement is a convenience only; the server re-derives the cap and the account scope from the token on every call (OpenAPI note C5). **Spoofing of freshness** - showing a stale number as current is the data-accuracy risk R7 for this ticket, addressed by the structural freshness pairing. No secret material is rendered, and key identifiers are truncated to `...{key_id_last4}` (SCR-079).

## Accessibility notes
SCR-079's rules: the drawer has a heading naming the account and its environment; balances are a description list with units; the permission summary is a list of plain statements ("Trade: yes. Withdrawal: off. IP allowlist: on."). Stale state is conveyed by the badge text, not by grey alone - the greying is reinforced with the "stale since" text. The leverage slider (CMP-104) is keyboard-operable with arrow and page keys, has a text input alternative, and announces its value and the applicable risk-limit tier. Toggles announce their state and the consequence of changing it. Exchange rejection messages are announced via `aria-live="assertive"`. Focus is trapped in the drawer and returns to the invoking control on close. Contrast >=4.5:1 in both themes.

## Performance notes
The drawer opens from cached state in <=100 ms and refreshes in place. The `wallet` topic is throttled to 500 ms by the protocol and uses whole-object last-write-wins, so the client applies snapshots rather than diffing. Leverage changes are user-initiated and bounded by the exchange round-trip; the control shows a pending state and must not block the drawer. No per-frame work: this screen must never contribute to the chart's frame budget.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_leverage_changes_total{result}`, `cv_margin_mode_changes_total{result}`, `cv_wallet_snapshot_age_seconds{account}` (reused from E27-T04).
Audit: `account.leverage_changed {account, symbol, before, after}` and `account.margin_mode_changed` (US-ACCT-009 NFR: "changes are audited"); `account.detail_viewed` as analytics only.
Frontend error boundary reports render failures with the screen ID SCR-079.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via PR <=400 LOC diff, conventional commits, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner; all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/accounts` and `candleviewer/credentials` (M2 is in the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; no field shipped that is not in the spec, no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: schema/API deltas noted in the PR description; runbook entry added when the change is operational.
- [ ] Observability (metrics, audit events) added and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off (E27-D06 handoff accepted, E27-D07 design QA passed) for any ticket touching UI.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E27-Q05.
- [ ] Secret-leak assertion suite from E27-T02/E27-X02 passes: no key material in logs, traces, metrics, error bodies or support bundles.

title: UX research: how the owner actually manages exchange keys, rotation and compromise
body:
## Context
E27 introduces an interaction the product has never had: handling credentials that can move real money, under a set of rules the user cannot change (withdrawal always off, IP allowlist mandatory, secrets never re-displayed, allowlist configurable only in Bybit's browser UI since Feb 2026). ADR-0009 states the design constraint that makes research necessary: "Rotation must be practical enough that it actually happens."

Before wireframes, we need evidence about how the owner and the account managers currently do this: where they keep keys, what they believe about what the app can see, what makes them avoid rotation, and what they would do first in a suspected compromise. The failure mode this research protects against is a flow that is technically correct and behaviourally ignored - keys that never rotate, allowlists never configured, and a compromise response improvised under stress.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Research plan and discussion guide covering: current key-handling practice, mental model of "the app has my keys", perceived cost of rotation, the 48-hour Bybit new-key restriction as a planning constraint, and a first-response walkthrough for suspected compromise.
- 5 to 6 sessions: the owner, 2 account managers (per the persona set in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`), and 2 to 3 comparable self-hosted-tool operators.
- A task-based think-aloud using a paper or Figma-lite mock of the rotation stepper and the revoke decision ("leave positions" versus "flatten first"), to observe which branch people pick under time pressure and why.
- Comprehension check on the three statements the UI must convey and that users typically get wrong: the secret can never be shown again; a database backup without the KEK is useless; the IP allowlist must be set in Bybit's dashboard, not here.
- Findings report with prioritised implications, each tied to a specific screen ID (SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129, SCR-079).
- A copy-deck seed: the exact wording candidates for the withdrawal verdict, the IP-mismatch remediation, the stale-balance badge and the irreversible-delete warning, to be validated in E27-D03.

## Out of scope
Visual design (E27-D02 and E27-D03); motion (E27-D04); usability testing of the built product (E27-Q04 exploratory charter); research on order entry or profiles (owned by E30 and E28).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sessions completed and synthesised
  Given the research plan is approved
  When the sessions have run
  Then at least 5 sessions are recorded and synthesised, and the findings report is published with prioritised implications

Scenario: Every implication is actionable
  When the findings report is reviewed
  Then each implication names the screen it affects, the decision it changes, and the confidence behind it

Scenario: Rotation avoidance is understood
  When participants are asked why they have not rotated keys before
  Then the reasons are categorised, and at least one concrete design response is proposed for each category

Scenario: The three hard facts are tested for comprehension
  Given the candidate copy for write-only secrets, KEK-separated backups and browser-only allowlists
  When participants read it and are asked to restate it
  Then comprehension is measured, and any statement misunderstood by more than one participant is rewritten and retested

Scenario: Research contradicts the plan
  Given a finding conflicts with a locked decision such as never re-displaying a secret
  Then the finding is recorded with its implication, the locked decision stands, and the design response is to explain rather than to change the rule
```

## Technical notes / design
Mixed methods: semi-structured interview plus task-based think-aloud. Sessions are 45 minutes, remote, recorded with consent. Analysis is thematic with two coders to reduce single-researcher bias. Sample size is small by necessity - the product has one owner and a few managers - so findings are reported as directional with explicit confidence levels rather than as statistics.

Prototype fidelity is deliberately low so that participants critique the flow rather than the visuals.

## Test plan
Validation is the comprehension check itself: candidate copy is accepted only when participants can restate it correctly in their own words. Findings feed directly into E27-D02's wireframe states and into the exploratory charter in E27-Q04.

## Security notes
No real API keys, UIDs or IP addresses are used in any prototype or discussion - placeholders only, stated to participants. Session recordings contain operational detail about how the owner secures credentials and are therefore **Confidential**: stored in the research repository with restricted access, and deleted after synthesis per the retention rule in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Participants are told explicitly that they must not read real credentials aloud.

## Accessibility notes
Recruit at least one participant who uses a screen reader or keyboard-only navigation, or run a parallel expert review with an accessibility specialist, so that the a11y implications of the stepper and the confirmation dialogs are grounded rather than assumed. Prototypes used in sessions must be keyboard-operable.

## Performance notes
N/A - no runtime performance implications. Perceived-time findings (how long users will tolerate a connection test before assuming failure) are captured and feed the <=3 s budget on SCR-126.

## Observability
N/A - no telemetry is produced by this ticket. The research does specify which analytics events would answer the open questions later: `admin.key_form_opened`, `admin.key_test_run`, `admin.key_health_viewed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Research plan approved by the Chief Design Officer before fieldwork.
- [ ] At least 5 sessions run, recorded with consent and synthesised by two coders.
- [ ] Findings report published with prioritised, screen-linked implications and stated confidence.
- [ ] Copy-deck seed handed to E27-D03.
- [ ] Recordings handled and deleted per the retention policy; no real credential appears in any artefact.
- [ ] Status Done at least 2 sprints before E27-S01 starts in Sprint 15.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09**, which establishes the authentication, step-up and RBAC model that the key-management flows sit inside; researching rotation without knowing whether step-up is required would produce findings we could not act on.

`design/e27-ux-research` - research artefacts committed under `docs/research/e27/`; no product code.

title: Wireframe SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079 with every state
body:
## Context
E27 introduces five admin screens and one trading-side drawer, all specified in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` with wireframes, states and per-screen sign-off checklists. This ticket produces the low-fidelity structure for all six, resolving layout and information hierarchy before any visual work, and - most importantly - drawing the **failure states as primary cases**, because in this epic the failure states are the point: a key with withdrawal permission, an IP allowlist that does not match, a stale balance, a rotation whose replacement key fails validation, and a delete blocked by open exposure.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes for **SCR-125** (accounts list): the column set label, UID, environment, permissions, IP allowlist, key age, state; the aggregate "Withdrawal permission: OFF on all accounts (verified <time>)" line and its negated form; per-row actions; empty state; and the withdrawal-permission-detected state drawn as a **blocking error, not a warning**.
- **SCR-126** (add / edit account): label, environment, write-only API key and secret fields, IP allowlist display, intended-permissions checklist, the "Test connection" result panel showing what the backend verified (UID, permissions, allowlist, server-time skew), a failure state per check, edit mode with an empty optional secret, and the step-up gate before save.
- **SCR-127** (key rotation): every stage of the wizard with its success and failure state; the "orders are drained before switch-over" behaviour stated; the rollback state when the new key fails validation; the reminder to delete the old key at Bybit with a confirmation checkbox; the key-age policy restated; the step-up gate.
- **SCR-128** (key health & secrets policy): per-key age, permissions, allowlist state and rotation-due date; the secrets-at-rest policy written as plain sentences; the "mark as compromised" emergency action with its immediate effect; the overdue state.
- **SCR-129** (disable / delete): disable and delete as separate flows with different copy; open positions, orders and algos blocking deletion and listed with counts; the statement that historical records are retained; assigned users listed with what they lose; typed confirmation plus step-up; the irreversibility of delete.
- **SCR-079** (account detail drawer): equity, available balance, used margin, unrealised PnL, leverage, position mode and margin mode with units; the permission and allowlist summary; the profile summary with an owner-only link to SCR-131; the rate-limit budget; the disabled or suspended account state; and the freshness and "stale since" treatment.
- A state inventory table listing every state per screen, cross-checked against the states named in the screens catalogue, so nothing is discovered missing during hi-fi.
- Information-hierarchy rationale for SCR-125: what must be readable at a glance versus on demand.

## Out of scope
Visual design, colour and type (E27-D03); motion (E27-D04); the design-system component contributions (E27-D03); Storybook implementation; anything relating to profiles (E28) or the order ticket (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued state is drawn
  Given the states named in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md for the six screens
  When the wireframe set is reviewed against the state inventory
  Then every state has a frame and no frame exists that is not in the inventory

Scenario: Failure states are primary
  When the wireframe set is reviewed
  Then the withdrawal-permission-detected, IP-mismatch, stale-balance, failed-replacement-key and blocked-delete states are drawn at the same fidelity as the happy path, not as annotations

Scenario: No secret is renderable
  When every frame is inspected
  Then no frame shows an API secret, and every key identifier is truncated

Scenario: The three hard facts are expressed
  When the frames for SCR-126, SCR-128 and SCR-129 are read
  Then each of the three facts from E27-D01 (write-only secrets, KEK-separated backups, browser-only allowlist) is stated in plain language on the screen where it matters

Scenario: A state has no home
  Given a backend state such as "within Bybit's 48 h new-key restriction" that no frame accommodates
  Then a frame is added or the state is explicitly deferred with a written rationale before sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Wireframes are greyscale and typographically neutral so that reviewers judge structure, not style. Each frame is annotated with: the data source (the exact API path or WS topic from the screens catalogue), the RBAC requirement, and the audit event the screen emits.

The layout must accommodate the real cardinality: at most 6 accounts in v1, which means SCR-125 should not be designed as a dense data grid optimised for hundreds of rows; the space is better spent on making state legible.

The SCR-126 result panel is structured as a list of checks with an outcome per check, because the screens catalogue requires that "the test result is a list, not a colour".

## Test plan
Design critique with engineering present, so that any state impossible to produce is caught early. Walk-through against each screen's own design sign-off acceptance checklist in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, item by item. Keyboard-path dry-run on paper: every action must have a keyboard route before hi-fi begins.

## Security notes
The design must make three security properties self-evident rather than merely true: that the app cannot see the secret after save, that withdrawal is off on every account, and that deleting an account does not close positions. Misrepresenting any of these in the visual language would be a security defect, not a cosmetic one. No real UIDs, keys or IPs appear in any frame. The Security engineer reviews the SCR-126, SCR-127 and SCR-128 frames.

## Accessibility notes

title: Hi-fi design and design-system contributions for the accounts and key-vault surfaces
body:
## Context
Turns the E27-D02 wireframes into signed-off high-fidelity design and contributes the components this epic introduces or extends to the shared design system, so that no screen ships a one-off control.

The epic touches 24 catalogued components, but only three are substantially defined by it: **CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge** (the visual language of the withdrawal, scope and allowlist verdicts), **CMP-176 AccountKeyRow** (the admin accounts table row) and **CMP-034 MaskedValue**, which this epic redefines - the catalogue calls it "secret reveal", but in CandleViewer there is **no reveal control anywhere in the app or API** (US-ACCT-002), so the component must be specified as permanently masked and the misleading name annotated.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for every state from the E27-D02 inventory across SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079, in dark (default) and light themes and all three densities.
- Design-system contributions with token bindings from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`:
  - **CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge** - variants for verified, trade-only, read-only, withdrawal-detected (critical), IP-missing, IP-mismatch, expiring and expired; each distinguishable in greyscale and under both common colour-vision deficiencies; each carrying its own text label.
  - **CMP-176 AccountKeyRow** - the composite row with label, UID, environment, permission badge, allowlist state, key age and health chip, including its blocked and disabled variants.
  - **CMP-034 MaskedValue** - respecified as permanently masked with no reveal affordance, showing `...{last4}` only, with a note recording why the reveal variant is deliberately absent.
- Extensions documented, not forked, for CMP-028 Callout/Banner (the blocking KEK-unavailable banner), CMP-035 Countdown (the rotation overlap), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog (typed-label confirmation plus step-up), CMP-066 Stepper (the rotation wizard) and CMP-178 SystemHealthTile (per-key health).
- The final copy deck for all six screens, validated against the E27-D01 comprehension findings: the withdrawal verdict, the IP-mismatch remediation including the instruction to set the allowlist in Bybit's dashboard, the stale-balance badge, the irreversible-delete warning, the "revoke and leave positions" versus "flatten first" choice, and the write-only secret explanation.
- Storybook story list per contributed component, handed to engineering.

## Out of scope
Motion specification (E27-D04); the a11y audit of the built screens (E27-D05); the handoff pack (E27-D06); design QA of the implementation (E27-D07); implementation itself.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Hi-fi covers both themes and all densities
  When the frame set is reviewed
  Then every state from the E27-D02 inventory exists in dark and light, and compact, cosy and comfortable densities are specified

Scenario: Key states survive greyscale and colour-vision deficiency
  Given the CMP-175 variants rendered in greyscale and under deuteranopia and protanopia simulation
  When they are compared
  Then each remains distinguishable and each carries a text label rather than relying on colour

Scenario: Withdrawal-detected reads as blocking
  Given the withdrawal-permission-detected state beside the ordinary warning states
  When a reviewer who has not seen the designs before is shown the accounts list
  Then they identify the blocking state without prompting

Scenario: MaskedValue has no reveal
  When CMP-034's specification is reviewed
  Then it defines no reveal affordance in any variant, and the rationale is recorded in the component entry

Scenario: Contrast
  When every text and graphical element is measured in both themes
  Then text is at least 4.5:1 and graphical boundaries at least 3:1 against their background

Scenario: A frame needs an element with no CMP entry
  Given a frame requires a control that does not exist in the catalogue
  Then a design-system contribution is raised and resolved before sign-off, and no one-off component ships
```

## Technical notes / design
All colour comes from tokens in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; nothing is hand-picked. The critical and warning states must be built from the existing `color.status.*` scale, extended through the design system if the scale proves insufficient rather than overridden locally.

Density matters more than usual on SCR-128, which is a table of keys with several state columns; the compact density must remain legible at 125% zoom.

Copy is part of this deliverable, not a later concern: this epic's screens are mostly explanation, and the E27-D01 comprehension findings determine the wording. Every string is written in the copy deck with its screen and element ID so engineering does not invent text.

## Test plan
Contrast measured with the design-system plugin on every foreground and background pair. Greyscale and colour-vision-deficiency simulation passes for all CMP-175 variants. The frame set is reviewed against each screen's own design sign-off acceptance checklist in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, and the review comment ticks them item by item. Copy is re-tested for comprehension with at least two people who were not in the E27-D01 sessions.

## Security notes
The visual language is a security control here. Misrepresentation is the threat: a withdrawal-detected state that reads as a mild warning, a stale balance that reads as current, or a masked value that implies a reveal is available would each cause a wrong decision. The Security engineer reviews and signs off the CMP-175 variant set and the SCR-126, SCR-127 and SCR-128 copy. No real UID, key or IP appears in any frame.

## Accessibility notes
Every state distinction is carried by text plus shape, never colour alone. Focus indicators are specified at >=3:1 contrast against both adjacent colours. Touch and click targets meet the minimum size in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. The permanently masked value has a programmatic description explaining that the value is write-only and cannot be revealed. Live-region behaviour specified for the health chips, the rotation countdown and exchange error messages. The layout is verified at 125% zoom and 200% text scaling without loss of content or function.

## Performance notes
Specify skeleton and loading treatments consistent with the perceived-performance budgets recorded in E27-D02, especially the SCR-126 validating state (<=3 s) and the SCR-129 consequence summary (<=1 s) during which the confirm control must not be present.

No runtime telemetry. The frames carry the audit and analytics annotations inherited from E27-D02 so that engineering implements them without re-deriving.

title: Specify motion and state-transition choreography for key verification, rotation and danger states
body:
## Context
This epic's screens are mostly about state changing over time - a connection test progressing check by check, a rotation moving through stages with a countdown, a health chip degrading, a balance going stale - and motion is how a user understands that something changed rather than that they misread it.

Motion here also carries risk: an animated transition on a destructive confirmation can make a dangerous action feel routine, and a spinner that hides per-check progress on SCR-126 turns a 3-second verification into an unexplained wait.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion specification for: the SCR-126 connection test revealing its checks progressively; the SCR-127 stepper advancing and rolling back; the CMP-035 rotation countdown; health-chip transitions on SCR-125 between healthy, degraded and down; the balance going stale on SCR-079; and the blocking KEK-unavailable banner appearing.
- Explicit anti-motion rules: destructive confirmations (SCR-129, revoke, mark-compromised) appear without decorative animation; the withdrawal-detected state does not fade in gently; nothing about a blocking error is soft.
- Durations, easing curves and stagger values expressed as design-system motion tokens, not one-off numbers.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for every specified transition: what becomes an instant state change and what, if anything, is retained as a non-motion cue.
- A statement of what must **not** animate: numeric balances never tween between values, because an intermediate frame of a balance is a number that was never true.

## Out of scope
Visual design (E27-D03); implementation; chart-engine animation, which is governed separately by `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`; motion for screens outside this epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every transition has a token-based specification
  When the motion spec is reviewed
  Then each listed transition has a duration, easing and stagger expressed in design-system motion tokens

Scenario: Reduced motion is complete
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  When each transition is reviewed
  Then each has a defined non-animated equivalent that preserves the information the motion conveyed

Scenario: Danger is not softened
  When the destructive confirmations are reviewed
  Then none uses decorative motion, and the blocking withdrawal-detected state appears immediately

Scenario: Balances never tween
  When the balance update specification is reviewed
  Then values change discretely, and no intermediate interpolated value is ever displayed

Scenario: Progressive verification is legible
  Given the connection test takes 3 seconds
  When the motion spec is applied
  Then each completed check is revealed as it completes rather than all at once at the end
```

## Technical notes / design
Motion tokens come from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`. Durations stay short - the guidance for functional state feedback is well under 200 ms - so that a user performing several key operations in sequence is never waiting on choreography.

The progressive reveal of verification checks is driven by real backend progress, not a simulated timeline; if the backend returns all checks at once, the reveal is a single step rather than a fake stagger, because a fabricated progress animation is a lie about system state.

## Test plan
Prototype the transitions in Figma and review them at 1x speed with engineering present. Verify the reduced-motion variants by walking every transition with the preference simulated. Confirm with engineering that each specified transition is implementable with CSS transitions or the existing animation utility, without a new dependency.

## Security notes
Motion must not be used to soften a security-relevant state. The specification explicitly forbids fading in the withdrawal-detected banner, animating the destructive confirmation entrance, or using motion to draw attention away from a failed check. Reviewed by the Security engineer alongside E27-D03.

## Accessibility notes
`prefers-reduced-motion` support is mandatory per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, and every transition here has a defined reduced equivalent. No transition may be the only indication that something changed - each is paired with a text or live-region change, so a user who cannot perceive motion loses nothing. No flashing above the seizure-safety threshold.

## Performance notes
Transitions are CSS-driven, composited properties only (transform and opacity), so they never trigger layout. Nothing in this epic animates per frame or competes with the chart's frame budget. Motion must not delay the availability of a control: an element is interactive from the start of its entrance.

## Observability
N/A - motion produces no telemetry.
