title: Accessibility design review of the six accounts and key-vault surfaces
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA as the floor, with axe-core in CI and manual screen-reader passes. This epic is unusually dependent on getting accessibility right at design time rather than fixing it later, because its screens communicate consequential state - a key that can withdraw, a balance that is stale, an account that cannot trade - and every one of those is the kind of thing that is usually conveyed by colour alone.

The screens catalogue already fixes several requirements per screen (text chips on SCR-125, a result list rather than a colour on SCR-126, a labelled stepper with `aria-current` on SCR-127, plain-sentence policy text on SCR-128, an `alertdialog` with focus starting on Cancel on SCR-129, a description list with units on SCR-079). This review verifies that the hi-fi design actually satisfies them before a line of code is written.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Annotated accessibility review of every hi-fi frame from E27-D03, producing a defect list with a named owner and a resolution for each item.
- Verification per screen against its catalogue requirement: SCR-125 text chips and explicit withdrawal verdict; SCR-126 write-only field description and result-as-list; SCR-127 stepper regions with `aria-current="step"`; SCR-128 plain-sentence policy and text-plus-icon warnings; SCR-129 `alertdialog` with the consequences restated as a list, typed confirmation and focus starting on Cancel; SCR-079 heading naming account and environment, balances as a description list with units, permission summary as plain statements.
- Focus-order map per screen and per dialog, including where focus goes on open, on close, on error and on step change.
- Live-region plan: what is announced politely (health transitions, countdown milestones), what assertively (exchange errors, blocking banners, failed checks), and what is not announced at all to avoid chatter.
- Keyboard-only walkthrough of every flow: register an account, import a key, run a test, rotate, revoke, disable, delete, change leverage - each completable with no pointer.
- Contrast audit results for every state in both themes, including focus indicators and disabled states.
- Screen-reader script: the expected announcement for each critical state, written out, so that the manual pass in E27-Q04 has a pass criterion rather than an opinion.

## Out of scope
The automated axe-core run against the built screens (E27-Q04); implementation fixes; accessibility work on screens outside this epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue a11y requirement is verified
  Given the per-screen accessibility requirements in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the hi-fi frames are reviewed
  Then each requirement is confirmed satisfied or raised as a defect with an owner

Scenario: No state relies on colour alone
  Given every state across the six screens
  When each is rendered in greyscale
  Then every state remains identifiable from text and shape

Scenario: Keyboard-only completion
  Given each of the eight flows in scope
  When they are walked with keyboard only in the prototype
  Then each completes without a pointer, and any trap or unreachable control is raised as a defect

Scenario: Focus starts safely on destructive dialogs
  When the SCR-129 dialog is reviewed
  Then focus starts on Cancel and the dialog uses role alertdialog with the consequences restated as a list

Scenario: Announcements are specified, not assumed
  When the live-region plan is reviewed
  Then every critical state has an expected announcement written out, and the politeness level is justified

Scenario: A requirement cannot be met as designed
  Given a frame that cannot satisfy a WCAG 2.2 AA criterion
  Then the design is changed, not waived, and the change is re-reviewed before sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Review method: heuristic evaluation against WCAG 2.2 AA using the project's standard checklist, plus a prototype walkthrough. The reviewer is an accessibility specialist from the design org, not the designer who produced the frames.

The live-region plan needs judgement rather than maximalism: this epic has several things that change on a timer (heartbeat age, countdown, staleness), and announcing all of them would make the screen unusable with a screen reader. The plan must state explicitly what is deliberately silent and why, with the information available on demand instead.

## Test plan
Contrast measured on every pair including focus and disabled states. Keyboard walkthrough executed and recorded. The screen-reader script is validated against at least one real screen reader on the prototype where feasible (NVDA on Windows is the project's primary target), with the full pass deferred to E27-Q04 on the built screens.

## Security notes
Two intersections with security matter here. First, the write-only secret field must have a programmatic description saying the value cannot be revealed, so that a screen-reader user is not left hunting for a reveal control that does not exist. Second, destructive confirmations must be equally clear non-visually: the consequences list, the typed-label requirement and the irreversibility must all be announced, so that a non-visual user is not at greater risk of an accidental deletion.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is itself the accessibility deliverable; see Scope. The output is the pass criterion used by E27-Q04's manual screen-reader audit and by E27-D07's design QA.

## Performance notes
Announcement frequency is a performance concern for assistive technology: the live-region plan caps announcements so that throttled updates (`wallet` at 500 ms, `system` at 1000 ms) do not produce a stream of speech. Only discrete transitions are announced, never every tick.

## Observability
N/A - no telemetry. The review does record which states must be observable in the UI for an operator to diagnose an issue without reading logs.

title: Produce and sign off the engineering handoff pack for the accounts and key-vault epic
body:
## Context
The design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` is explicit: no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off, with Status Done on the design ticket. This is the ticket whose completion unblocks E27-S01 through E27-S05, so it must be genuinely complete - a developer picking up SCR-126 should not need to ask a designer anything.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A single handoff pack covering SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079, linked from every consuming engineering ticket.
- Per screen: the final frame set with every state, redlines or the equivalent token annotations, the component inventory naming each CMP ID used, the data sources (exact API paths and WS topics), the RBAC requirement, and the audit and analytics events to emit.
- The final copy deck with every string keyed by screen and element, including all error and empty-state text, so no text is invented during implementation.
- The contributed design-system entries for CMP-175, CMP-176 and CMP-034 published in the library with their Storybook story lists.
- The focus-order maps, live-region plan and screen-reader scripts from E27-D05.
- The motion specification from E27-D04 with its reduced-motion equivalents.
- A written statement of the epic's non-negotiable visual rules: no reveal control for secrets anywhere; the withdrawal verdict is always explicit; no numeric value is shown without its freshness; destructive actions require typed confirmation plus step-up.
- A 45-minute handoff walkthrough with the frontend engineers who will build the screens, with questions captured and answered in the pack rather than in chat.
- A sign-off record listing the Chief Design Officer or delegate, the accessibility specialist and the Security engineer.

## Out of scope
Design QA of the built implementation (E27-D07); changes arising from implementation discoveries, which are handled as follow-up design tickets; implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The pack is self-sufficient
  Given a frontend engineer who has not attended any design review
  When they build SCR-126 from the pack alone
  Then they need no clarification from the design team, evidenced by zero design questions raised during the ticket

Scenario: Every string is in the copy deck
  When the implementation is compared to the copy deck
  Then every rendered string is present in the deck and no string was invented during implementation

Scenario: Sign-offs are complete before engineering starts
  When E27-S01 enters In Progress
  Then this ticket is already Done with all three sign-offs recorded, at least two sprints earlier

Scenario: Components come from the library
  When the built screens are inspected
  Then every control resolves to a catalogued CMP entry, and no one-off component exists

Scenario: A gap is found during implementation
  Given an engineer finds a state with no frame
  Then a follow-up design ticket is raised, the pack is updated, and the gap is recorded so the handoff checklist can be improved
```

## Technical notes / design
The pack lives in Figma with a committed index under `docs/design/e27/handoff.md` that links each screen to its frames, its copy-deck section and its component entries - so the authoritative pointer survives even if the Figma structure is reorganised.

Redlines are minimised in favour of token references: an engineer should read "spacing.md, color.status.critical" rather than a pixel value, because that is what makes the implementation stay consistent when tokens change.

## Test plan
Validation is the handoff walkthrough itself plus the self-sufficiency criterion above: design questions raised during E27-S01 to E27-S05 are counted, and any question that should have been answered by the pack is logged as an improvement to the handoff checklist. A link-checker validates every reference in the committed index.

## Security notes
The pack restates the epic's security-relevant visual rules explicitly, so that an engineer cannot implement a reveal affordance, a colour-only withdrawal verdict or a freshness-free balance by accident. The Security engineer's sign-off on the pack is required, not optional.

## Accessibility notes
The pack carries the full E27-D05 output - focus-order maps, live-region plan and screen-reader scripts - so that accessibility is implemented from a specification rather than retrofitted after an axe-core failure.

## Performance notes
The pack records the perceived-performance budgets per screen: SCR-126 <=3 s test round-trip with a validating state, SCR-127 <=10 s rotation with per-stage timing, SCR-129 <=1 s consequence summary before the confirm control appears, SCR-079 <=100 ms open from cache, SCR-125 health refresh every 60 s and never per second.

The pack lists, per screen, the audit events (`account.created`, `account.updated`, `account.tested`, `account.disabled_by_policy`, `account.key_rotated`, `account.key_revoked`, `admin.secrets_policy_changed`, `admin.key_marked_compromised`) and the analytics events (`admin.accounts_list_viewed`, `admin.key_form_opened`, `admin.key_test_run`, `admin.key_health_viewed`, `account.detail_viewed`) that implementation must emit.

title: Design QA the implemented accounts and key-vault screens against the handoff pack
body:
## Context
Design QA closes the loop: the built screens are compared against the E27-D06 handoff pack, state by state, in both themes and all densities, on real data from the demo environment. R3's quality gate names it directly - "design-QA on ticket, confirmation and danger states" - and this epic's danger states are exactly where a drift between design and implementation would matter most.

It runs in Sprint 16, after the five E27 stories land in Sprint 15, so that it inspects finished screens rather than work in progress.

## Scope / Deliverables
- State-by-state comparison of SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079 against the handoff pack, in dark and light themes and compact, cosy and comfortable densities.
- Verification of the epic's non-negotiable visual rules on the running application: no reveal control exists anywhere for a secret; the withdrawal verdict is always explicit and text-based; no numeric value renders without its freshness; destructive actions require typed confirmation plus step-up.
- Copy verification: every rendered string matches the copy deck exactly, including error and empty-state text.
- Token verification: spacing, colour, type and motion resolve to design-system tokens, with no hard-coded values, checked in the DOM rather than by eye.
- Motion verification including the `prefers-reduced-motion` variants, and confirmation that balances do not tween.
- Defect list with severity, each linked to the screen and state, triaged with engineering and fixed before the epic closes.
- A short drift report noting anything the implementation revealed that the design got wrong, feeding the next epic's handoff checklist.

## Out of scope
Functional QA (E27-Q01 to E27-Q05); the accessibility audit (E27-Q04); security review (E27-X02); redesign work, which is raised as follow-up design tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state matches the pack
  Given the handoff pack's state inventory
  When each state is reproduced in the running app in both themes and all densities
  Then it matches the design, or a defect is raised with a screenshot and the exact discrepancy

Scenario: No reveal control exists
  Given the running application and its API
  When every screen showing a key, and every API response, is inspected
  Then no reveal affordance and no secret value is present anywhere

Scenario: Freshness is always present
  Given the SCR-079 drawer with live and with stale data
  When every numeric field is inspected
  Then each carries a freshness indicator, and the stale state shows the "stale since" badge

Scenario: Copy matches the deck
  When every rendered string is compared to the copy deck
  Then they match exactly, and any difference is raised as a defect rather than accepted as an improvement

Scenario: Tokens, not values
  When the DOM is inspected for the six screens
  Then spacing, colour, type and motion resolve to design-system tokens with no hard-coded values

Scenario: A defect is disputed
  Given engineering believes a discrepancy is intentional
  Then it is resolved by the Chief Design Officer or delegate before the epic closes, and the decision is recorded in the drift report
```

## Technical notes / design
Design QA is performed on the demo environment with real account data, not on Storybook alone, because several states in this epic only occur against real exchange responses - the 48-hour new-key restriction, an IP mismatch, a genuinely stale wallet snapshot.

Storybook is still used for the component-level check of CMP-175, CMP-176 and CMP-034 variants, where reproducing every state in the app would be impractical.

Hard-to-reach states are produced with the fault-injection fixtures built for E27-Q01 rather than by waiting for them to occur naturally.

## Test plan
Checklist-driven review executed by a product designer who did not implement the screens, with engineering available. Screenshot evidence captured for every state. Results recorded in `qa/design-qa/e27/` and linked here.

## Security notes
Design QA is the last chance to catch a visual security defect before the epic closes: a masked value that reveals on hover, an error toast that echoes a submitted secret, a withdrawal verdict rendered as a colour-only chip, or a screenshot path that captures credential input. Each of these is checked explicitly and, if found, raised at high severity. Findings overlap deliberately with E27-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Design QA includes a visual accessibility pass - focus indicators present and at >=3:1 contrast on every interactive element, disabled states distinguishable, states identifiable in greyscale, and the layout intact at 125% zoom and 200% text scaling. The full screen-reader and axe-core audit is E27-Q04; this pass catches the visual subset.

## Performance notes
Spot-check the perceived-performance budgets on the running app: the SCR-126 validating state appearing promptly and resolving within about 3 s, SCR-129's confirm control absent until the summary loads, and SCR-079 opening in about 100 ms from cache.

## Observability
Verify that the audit and analytics events listed in the handoff pack actually fire from the screens - a missing `account.tested` or `admin.key_health_viewed` is a defect found here as easily as in functional QA, and is raised the same way.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every state compared and evidenced with a screenshot.
- [ ] Defect list triaged with engineering; all high-severity items fixed before the epic closes.
- [ ] Copy and token verification complete.
- [ ] Drift report written and fed into the handoff checklist for the next epic.
- [ ] Signed off by the Chief Design Officer or delegate.
- [ ] Results committed under `qa/design-qa/e27/` and linked from this ticket.

Blocked by all five implementation stories (**E27-S01** to **E27-S05**) and by **E27-D06**, which is the specification it reviews against.

title: Write the black-box test plan and fault-injection fixtures for accounts and the key vault
body:
## Context
E27 is the epic where a functional defect can cost real money: an account that appears verified while its key carries withdrawal permission, a rotation that silently leaves the old key primary, a revoke that reports success while credentials survive, or a wallet snapshot presented as current when it is minutes old. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature group written independently of the implementation, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7.3 makes R3 exit criteria #9 and #10 (KEK separation demonstrated; withdrawal-enabled keys refused) gate-blocking.

Most of the interesting states in this epic cannot be produced on demand against the real exchange - the Bybit 48-hour new-key restriction, an IP-allowlist mismatch, a withdrawal-enabled key, a dead private WS, a clock skew beyond `recv_window`. This ticket therefore delivers both the plan and the **fixtures that make the plan executable**, so every other QA ticket in E27 (and the design QA in E27-D07) can reach those states deterministically.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Black-box test plan committed at `qa/plans/e27/test-plan.md`, written from `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` SS2 (US-ACCT-001..010) and the screen specs (SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129, SCR-079), **without reading the implementation**.
- Test-case suites, one per story group, each case with preconditions, steps, expected result, evidence to capture and the US id it covers:
  - **Registration** (US-ACCT-001): main account, sub-account, duplicate UID in the same environment, same UID in the other environment (must be allowed), the 6th sub-account cap with acknowledgement, label uniqueness per environment, RBAC (manager cannot register).
  - **Key intake** (US-ACCT-002, US-ACCT-003, US-ACCT-007): compliant key; withdrawal-enabled key (hard block); missing IP allowlist; egress IP not in the allowlist; UID mismatch against `exchange_accounts.exchange_uid`; non-UTA account; clock skew beyond `recv_window`; a live key pasted into a demo-bound account; key expiring inside 14 days (warning, not block); re-open the record and confirm no reveal control exists anywhere in UI or API.
  - **Rotation and policy** (US-ACCT-004, US-ACCT-005): happy-path overlap; replacement key failing verification (promotion refused, old key stays primary); early revoke of the old key; open orders not cancelled by rotation; amber chip at 76/90 days; red chip and daily alert when overdue; trading never auto-disabled for age alone; policy changed to 180 days recomputes immediately.
  - **Revoke, disable, delete** (US-ACCT-006): revoke with step-up; revoke with open positions through both branches ("revoke and leave positions", "flatten first, then revoke"); Bybit delete call failing while local deletion still succeeds; rules scoped to the account disarmed and listed; typed-label confirmation on delete; historical records retained.
  - **Health, balance and leverage** (US-ACCT-008, US-ACCT-009, US-ACCT-010): freshness timestamp always present; WS silent 60 s triggers REST reconciliation; both failing greys the figures and disables risk-based sizing; green/amber/red transitions with the <=30 s red deadline; order entry disabled for a red account; leverage set, leverage blocked by an open position, leverage above the profile cap refused before any exchange call.
- **Fault-injection fixture pack** at `packages/fixtures/accounts/`, replayable by the synthetic feed (`CV_FEED=synthetic`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS7.3): canned `GET /v5/user/query-api` responses for every verification verdict, a `wallet-balance` probe returning `retCode != 0`, a skewed-clock response, a WS that authenticates then drops, a Bybit 5xx and a `10018` rate-limit response, plus a 48-hour-restriction response.
- A coverage matrix in the plan mapping every case to its US id, proving all ten ACCT stories are covered and identifying which cases are automated (E27-Q02) versus manual.
- Defect-reporting convention for the epic, including the rule that any case producing visible secret material is raised as P0 regardless of other impact.

## Out of scope
- Writing the automated E2E specs themselves - that is E27-Q02, which consumes this plan.
- Accessibility auditing (E27-Q04), load and chaos work (E27-Q03), security review (E27-X01..X04).
- White-box unit tests, which ship with their implementation tickets.
- Testing profiles and trade groups (E28) or the OMS (E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Must/Should story has executable coverage
  Given qa/plans/e27/test-plan.md is complete
  When the coverage matrix is reviewed against docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 2
  Then each of US-ACCT-001 to US-ACCT-010 maps to at least one positive case and one negative/failure case, and no case is marked "cannot be executed"

Scenario: A hostile key state can be produced on demand
  Given the fixture pack is installed and the synthetic feed is selected
  When a tester selects the "withdrawal enabled" fixture and submits a key
  Then the verification pipeline rejects it with code validation_failed / key_withdraw_permission, and the tester reached that state without touching the real exchange

Scenario: Freshness is testable
  Given the "WS authenticates then drops" fixture is active
  When 60 seconds pass with no wallet frame
  Then the plan's expected result - REST reconciliation runs and the freshness timestamp updates - can be observed and evidenced, and a further failure produces the greyed "stale since <time>" state

Scenario: The plan is implementation-independent
  When the plan is reviewed by the engineer who implemented E27-T03
  Then no case refers to an internal function, module path or private field; every case is expressed in terms of the UI or the documented API contract

## Technical notes / design
The fixture pack is structured as one directory per verdict with a `manifest.json` naming the scenario, the endpoints it stubs and the expected UI outcome, so a tester selects a scenario by name (`CV_ACCOUNT_FIXTURE=withdraw_enabled`) rather than editing JSON. Stubs are served by the existing synthetic-feed harness, which already intercepts the exchange adapter's REST and WS clients; no production code path is modified to support testing.

Fixtures contain only fabricated UIDs, fabricated key-id prefixes and RFC 5737 documentation IP addresses. A CI check greps the fixture directory for anything resembling a real 20-character Bybit key and fails the build if found - fixtures are committed to the repository, so this is a hard requirement rather than a convention.

Each case in the plan carries a stable id (`E27-TC-nnn`) used by the automated specs in E27-Q02, the regression pack in E27-Q05 and defect reports, so traceability survives refactors of the plan's prose.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* test artefact production. Its own verification is a peer review by the second QA/SDET engineer plus a dry run: each fixture is loaded once against the running demo stack and confirmed to produce the state it claims. The dry-run log is committed alongside the plan as evidence. Fixture manifests are schema-validated in CI so a malformed manifest fails fast.

## Security notes
Fixtures must never contain real credentials, real UIDs or the deployment's real egress IP - enforced by the CI grep described above and by review. The plan's expected results encode security behaviour as testable statements (no reveal control exists; a rejected key is never persisted; local deletion is authoritative), which is what turns the security requirements of ADR-0009 into something QA can fail the build on. Classification of the artefacts: Internal.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes an accessibility column flagging which cases must also be executed keyboard-only, but the full audit is E27-Q04. Test-plan documents themselves follow the repository's Markdown accessibility conventions (real headings, tables with header rows, no meaning conveyed by colour alone).

## Performance notes
The plan records the perceived-performance expectations from the screen specs as observable assertions - SCR-126's validation round-trip at <=3 s, SCR-127's rotation at <=10 s, SCR-079 opening in <=100 ms from cache, SCR-125 health refreshing every 60 s and never per second - so that a regression in these is a functional defect, not only a perf-ticket concern. Load testing is E27-Q03.

## Observability
Each case names the audit event it expects (`account.created`, `account.updated`, `account.tested`, `account.key_rotated`, `account.disabled`, `account.deleted`, `account.disabled_by_policy`) so a missing audit row is caught as a functional defect. The plan also lists the metrics a tester should see move (`cv_account_health_state`, `cv_key_verification_total`) when executing the relevant cases.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e27/` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Every listed case executed with a recorded pass/fail result and evidence; defects raised with exact reproduction steps and fixtures.
- [ ] Automated cases added to the CI suite and green on `main` on two consecutive runs.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 defects for E27; P2s triaged with named owners and target sprints.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment recorded on the epic E27.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-T01** (the schema and domain model must exist for fixtures to be meaningful) and **E27-D02** (wireframed states define the expected results the plan asserts). Feeds E27-Q02, E27-Q04, E27-Q05 and E27-D07.

title: Automate the accounts and key-vault E2E suite in Playwright against the demo environment
body:
## Context
The five E27 stories each carry an E2E case in their own test plans; this ticket turns those into a maintained suite that runs on every PR and guards the epic against regression for the rest of the project's life. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E at the top of the pyramid with Playwright for web and Electron, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7.4 requires the R3 quality gates to hold continuously, not just at the gate.

The suite matters beyond E27: every later trading epic (E28 profiles, E29 OMS, E34 fan-out) assumes accounts can be registered, keyed, verified and health-checked. A break here is a break in the precondition of half the R3 train.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `apps/web/e2e/accounts/`, one file per flow, each case tagged with the `E27-TC-nnn` id from `qa/plans/e27/test-plan.md`:
  - `register-account.spec.ts` - register a demo sub-account through SCR-126, confirm it appears on SCR-125 as "no key - inactive", confirm duplicate UID rejection copy names the existing label, confirm the sub-account cap acknowledgement at the 6th.
  - `key-intake.spec.ts` - import a compliant demo key end to end and reach `verified`; attempt a withdrawal-enabled key and assert the hard block with the verbatim reason; attempt a key with no IP allowlist; assert the secret field is `type=password`, is never populated on edit, and that no response body anywhere in the flow contains the submitted secret.
  - `rotation.spec.ts` - rotate a demo key through the SCR-127 stepper, assert traffic switches and the old key is revoked at the end of the overlap; run the failed-replacement path and assert promotion is refused and the old key remains primary.
  - `revoke-and-delete.spec.ts` - revoke with step-up; revoke with an open position through the "flatten first" branch; disable and delete through SCR-129 with typed-label confirmation; assert dependent rules are listed and disarmed.
  - `account-health.spec.ts` - drive the fixture WS drop and assert the SCR-125 chip and SCR-079 drawer move green -> amber -> red inside the documented deadlines, and that order entry is disabled for a red account.
  - `leverage.spec.ts` - set leverage within the profile cap, then attempt to exceed it and assert client- and server-side refusal before any exchange call.
- Shared fixtures: a Playwright `accountsFixture` that seeds accounts through the API, a step-up helper that completes TOTP with a deterministic test secret, and a scenario selector that activates the E27-Q01 fault-injection fixtures per test.
- Deterministic teardown that removes created accounts and keys so the suite is re-runnable on the same demo environment without manual cleanup.
- CI wiring: the suite runs on PRs touching `apps/web/src/features/admin-accounts`, `admin-keys` or `services/api/candleviewer/admin`, and in the nightly full-E2E job; flake budget and quarantine policy per `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Out of scope
- Unit and contract tests (owned by the implementation tickets).
- Load, soak and chaos scenarios (E27-Q03) and the accessibility audit (E27-Q04).
- Running against `live` - E2E never touches live, per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS7.3.
- Electron-shell-specific coverage, which is owned by the desktop epic; these specs must nonetheless be shell-agnostic so they can be reused there.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The suite is green and stable
  Given the accounts E2E suite is wired into CI
  When it runs ten consecutive times against the demo environment
  Then it passes every time with no quarantined test, and total wall-clock runtime stays under 8 minutes

Scenario: A regression in the withdrawal block fails the build
  Given a deliberate regression that accepts a withdrawal-enabled key is introduced on a branch
  When the suite runs
  Then key-intake.spec.ts fails with a message naming the withdrawal check, and the PR cannot merge

Scenario: No secret ever crosses the wire back to the client
  Given key-intake.spec.ts records every network response during the flow
  When the assertions run
  Then no response body, header or WS frame contains the submitted secret or any substring of it longer than the masked prefix

Scenario: The suite cleans up after itself
  Given the suite has run once against a demo environment
  When it runs again immediately
  Then it passes without manual cleanup, because teardown removed every account, key and rule it created

## Technical notes / design
Specs drive the UI only - no direct database manipulation - except in `beforeAll` seeding, which uses the public API with an owner session so the suite exercises the same RBAC path a human would. The step-up helper computes TOTP codes from a test secret injected through the demo environment's seed data; it never hard-codes a code, because the window would make the suite flaky.

Network assertions use Playwright's `page.on('response')` plus a WS frame recorder, with the collected transcript scanned for the submitted secret at the end of the test. This is the E2E-level counterpart of the unit-level leak assertion from E27-T02 and is deliberately redundant with it: they fail for different reasons.

Timing-sensitive health assertions (green -> amber -> red) use fixture-controlled clocks where possible and generous upper bounds where not, asserting "within the deadline" rather than an exact instant, to keep the suite deterministic without weakening the requirement.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the test deliverable. Its verification is the ten-consecutive-run stability check above, a review by the engineer who owns each consuming story confirming the spec asserts the story's acceptance criteria faithfully, and a mutation check: for three chosen behaviours (withdrawal block, rotation refusal, leverage cap) a deliberate regression is introduced locally and the corresponding spec is confirmed to fail.

## Security notes
The test TOTP secret and the demo credentials used by CI live in the CI secret store, never in the repository - secrets scanning in CI enforces this. The suite's network transcripts are attached to failed runs as artefacts; the collector redacts anything matching the credential patterns before upload so a failing test never publishes a key into CI logs. Classification: Internal; the demo environment holds no real money but its keys are still Secret.

## Accessibility notes
Each spec includes at least one keyboard-only path (tab to the primary action and activate with Enter) so that gross keyboard regressions are caught continuously; the comprehensive audit remains E27-Q04. `@axe-core/playwright` is invoked on SCR-125, SCR-126 and SCR-127 with violations reported as test failures at the `serious` and `critical` levels.

## Performance notes
The suite asserts the user-visible timing budgets as soft bounds with generous headroom (SCR-126 validation resolving, SCR-127 rotation completing, SCR-079 opening), so a 10x regression fails while normal variance does not. Precise measurement belongs to E27-Q03.

## Observability
Failed runs upload the Playwright trace, the redacted network transcript and the backend structured logs for the run window, so a flake can be diagnosed without re-running. The suite emits its own pass/fail and duration metrics into the CI dashboard used for the epic's quality reporting.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e27/` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Every listed case executed with a recorded pass/fail result and evidence; defects raised with exact reproduction steps and fixtures.
- [ ] Automated cases added to the CI suite and green on `main` on two consecutive runs.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 defects for E27; P2s triaged with named owners and target sprints.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment recorded on the epic E27.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-Q01** (the plan and fixtures it automates) and by the four story tickets whose UI it drives - **E27-S02**, **E27-S03**, **E27-S04**, **E27-S05**. E27-S01 is implicitly required and is already a dependency of those stories.

title: Run the load, soak and chaos scenarios for account health, key verification and rate limits
body:
## Context
E27's runtime surface is small in request volume but sits on the critical path of everything else: the health monitor polls per account, the nightly self-check calls Bybit for every stored key, and the wallet snapshot cache feeds the drawer, the order ticket and risk-based sizing. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` requires load and chaos scenarios for high-consequence paths, and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS4.3 makes per-account rate-limit budgeting an architectural concern - a self-check storm that consumes the account's budget would degrade order placement, which is the one thing that must never happen.

R3's gate includes a seven-day soak (roadmap SS7.5, `q09`). This ticket produces the account-layer scenarios that soak must exercise and the evidence that the health monitor does not drift, leak or storm over days.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 scripts under `infra/k6/accounts/`:
  - `health-poll.js` - steady-state load with 6 accounts (the v1 maximum: main + 5 subs) polling health at the documented 60 s cadence, asserting `GET /exchange-accounts` p95 latency and that the exchange is never called more than the cache policy allows.
  - `key-verify-burst.js` - all stored keys re-verified simultaneously (the nightly job's worst case), measuring the exchange-call rate against the per-UID budget and asserting the order path's reserved budget is untouched.
  - `wallet-fanout.js` - private `wallet` WS frames at the documented 500 ms throttle across all accounts with 5 concurrent browser connections, asserting no unbounded queue growth and that coalescing behaves as `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS said (whole-object last-write-wins).
- Chaos scenarios, scripted and documented at `qa/plans/e27/chaos.md`, each with an expected system response and a pass criterion:
  - Private WS dropped and refused for 5 minutes: accounts go amber then red inside the deadlines, order entry disables, the dead-man's-switch policy is invoked, and full recovery occurs on reconnect without a restart.
  - Bybit REST returning 5xx for 2 minutes during a self-check: self-check fails closed, the account's prior verdict is retained with an explicit staleness marker, and no account is silently marked verified.
  - Rate-limit `10018` returned to the self-check path: backoff engages, the order path is unaffected, and a metric records the throttle.
  - Clock skew injected beyond `recv_window`: verification fails with the clock reason rather than a generic error, and the health panel says so.
  - KEK made unavailable at runtime (simulating a lost credential): the app enters the degraded read-only state from US-ACCT-002, refuses trading routes, shows the blocking banner, and recovers cleanly when the KEK returns.
- A 24-hour mini-soak of the health monitor in the demo environment ahead of the R3 seven-day soak, with a memory and task-count trend showing no growth.
- Results written to `qa/results/e27/` with the measured numbers against the budgets and a go/no-go statement for the epic.

## Out of scope
- Order-path and fan-out load testing (E29, E34) and ingestion soak (E17).
- Fixing any defects found - those are raised as separate Bug tickets against the owning implementation ticket.
- Live-environment testing of any kind.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Steady-state health polling is cheap
  Given 6 accounts are registered and healthy
  When health-poll.js runs for 30 minutes
  Then GET /exchange-accounts p95 stays within the API budget in docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md, and the exchange is called no more often than the 60-second cache policy permits

Scenario: A verification burst does not starve the order path
  Given all stored keys are re-verified simultaneously
  When key-verify-burst.js runs
  Then the per-UID exchange budget reserved for order placement is never consumed by verification, and a simultaneous order-path probe sees no added latency beyond the documented tolerance

Scenario: Losing the exchange fails closed, not open
  Given Bybit REST returns 5xx for two minutes during a scheduled self-check
  When the scenario runs
  Then no account transitions to "verified" on the failed check, the previous verdict is shown with an explicit staleness marker, and a critical alert is raised

Scenario: Losing the KEK degrades safely
  Given the KEK is made unavailable while the service is running
  When the next credential borrow is attempted
  Then the service enters read-only degraded mode, all trading routes refuse with the documented error, the blocking banner appears, and no plaintext credential is recoverable from memory dumps taken during the window

Scenario: The monitor does not drift over a day
  Given the 24-hour mini-soak has completed
  Then resident memory, open connections and asyncio task counts show no upward trend beyond noise, and every account's health state at the end matches its true state

## Technical notes / design
k6 drives the REST surface; the WS scenario uses the project's existing WS load harness rather than k6's limited WS support. Chaos is injected with the fault-injection fixtures from E27-Q01 plus network-level interference (`tc netem` / proxy kill) inside the compose stack, so the application is genuinely unaware it is being tested.

The "order path unaffected" assertion is measured with a low-rate probe placing and immediately cancelling demo orders throughout the burst; if E29 is not yet far enough along when this runs, the probe degrades to a signed read-only call on the same budget class, and the ticket records that substitution explicitly rather than silently.

The KEK-loss scenario is coordinated with Security (E27-X04) because it doubles as the availability half of the ADR-0009 restore drill.

## Test plan
This ticket is itself the test. Evidence is the committed k6 output, Grafana screenshots covering each scenario window, and the soak trend charts. Each chaos scenario is executed at least twice to confirm the response is deterministic rather than lucky.

## Security notes
The KEK-loss scenario is security-relevant and is reviewed jointly with the Security engineer: the pass criterion includes taking a process memory dump during the degraded window and confirming no plaintext credential is present, which is a direct test of ADR-0009's "plaintext exists only for the lifetime of a request signature" claim. Load-test configuration must never point at `live`; a guard in the scripts refuses to run when the target host matches the live API host. Classification: Internal.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface is exercised by this ticket. Accessibility of the health surfaces is covered by E27-Q04.

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: `GET /exchange-accounts` p95 within the API latency budget of `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; health refresh no more frequent than 60 s (SCR-125 note); wallet frames at the 500 ms throttle; SCR-079 drawer open <=100 ms from cache; SCR-126 verification round-trip <=3 s; SCR-127 rotation <=10 s total. Any budget missed is recorded with the measured number rather than rounded away, and either fixed or accepted with the Architect's written agreement.

## Observability
Scenarios assert that the epic's metrics move correctly under stress - `cv_account_health_state`, `cv_key_verification_total{result}`, `cv_exchange_rate_limit_remaining{uid}` and the credential-borrow counter - because a health monitor whose telemetry lies under load is worse than one with no telemetry. Alert rules for "account red for more than 60 s" and "self-check failing" are validated by these scenarios firing them for real.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e27/` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Every listed case executed with a recorded pass/fail result and evidence; defects raised with exact reproduction steps and fixtures.
- [ ] Automated cases added to the CI suite and green on `main` on two consecutive runs.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 defects for E27; P2s triaged with named owners and target sprints.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment recorded on the epic E27.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-T04** (the health monitor, policy evaluator and wallet cache are the subjects under test) and **E27-Q01** (fault-injection fixtures). Coordinates with **E27-X04** on the KEK-loss drill.

`chore/e27-load-chaos` - scripts under `infra/k6/accounts/` and docs under `qa/`; no production code changes.

title: Audit accessibility and run an exploratory charter across the six accounts and key-vault screens
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` binds the project to WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI and manual screen-reader passes, and the DoD in `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS2.2 makes that an epic-level gate for any epic with UI surface. E27 introduces six surfaces, several of which convey safety-critical verdicts - "withdrawal permission detected", "IP mismatch", "account red, order entry disabled" - that must be perceivable without colour and announced to a screen-reader user at the moment they change (US-ACCT-010 NFR: "states announced to screen readers via a live region").

Scripted tests only find what they were told to look for. This ticket pairs the audit with a time-boxed exploratory charter, which on an epic like this is where the interesting defects live: a masked field that reveals under autofill, a rotation wizard that loses focus between steps, a confirmation dialog that can be dismissed with Escape while a destructive request is already in flight.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated audit**: `@axe-core/playwright` run against SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079 in every documented state (empty, loading, populated, each error/verdict state, degraded), in dark and light themes and all three densities. Violations at `serious`/`critical` are defects; `moderate` are triaged.
- **Manual screen-reader passes**: NVDA + Firefox (primary), and one VoiceOver + Safari pass, executed against the script written in E27-D05 so each pass has a stated expected announcement rather than an opinion. Covered explicitly: the verification result list on SCR-126; `aria-current="step"` progression through the SCR-127 stepper; the `role="alertdialog"` consequence list on SCR-129; the live-region announcement when an account's health changes; the "value is write-only" description on the secret fields.
- **Keyboard-only pass**: every flow completed with no pointer - register, key intake with step-up, full rotation, revoke, disable/delete, leverage change - checking focus order, visible focus at >=3:1 contrast, no keyboard traps in dialogs and drawers, Escape semantics that never abandon an in-flight destructive request, and focus return to the invoking control on close.
- **Contrast and zoom**: measured contrast for every text and non-text pair including disabled and focus states; layout and function intact at 200% text scaling and 400% zoom / 320 CSS px reflow.
- **Exploratory charters** (2 sessions x 90 minutes, session notes committed): charter 1 - "try to make the app show me a secret, or make it believe an unsafe key is safe"; charter 2 - "interrupt every flow at its worst moment (navigate away mid-verification, double-submit rotation, revoke while a rotation overlaps, lose the network during delete) and find a state that lies".
- Audit report at `qa/a11y/e27/report.md` with every finding, its WCAG success criterion, severity, and the owning ticket; plus a re-test record after fixes.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the defects found - each is raised as a Bug against the owning story and fixed there.
- Screens outside E27 (profiles SCR-130/131 belong to E28; the audit method is shared).
- The design-time accessibility review, which is E27-D05 and is this ticket's input.
- Security review (E27-X02), though overlapping findings are handed over rather than duplicated.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No automated violations survive
  Given axe-core has run against all six screens in every documented state
  When the report is compiled
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations outstanding, and every moderate finding is either fixed or recorded with a written justification accepted by the accessibility lead

Scenario: A safety verdict is perceivable without colour
  Given a key with withdrawal permission enabled has been submitted
  When a screen-reader user reaches the result
  Then the failure is announced as text naming the withdrawal permission, the account's disabled-for-trading consequence is announced, and the same information is readable with colour removed

Scenario: Health changes are announced, not just repainted
  Given an account transitions from connected to down
  When the change occurs while the accounts list is open
  Then a polite live region announces the account label and its new state within one update cycle, and the row's chip text changes, not only its colour

Scenario: A destructive dialog cannot be escaped into ambiguity
  Given the delete confirmation is open and the request has been submitted
  When Escape is pressed
  Then the dialog does not close into an unknown state; it either blocks dismissal until the outcome is known or reports the outcome explicitly afterwards

Scenario: Exploration is evidenced
  When the two exploratory sessions are complete
  Then session notes list every path taken and every anomaly observed, and each anomaly is either raised as a defect or explicitly dismissed with a reason

## Technical notes / design
The audit runs against the built application on the demo environment, not Storybook, because several states only occur against real exchange responses; Storybook is used for component-level checks of CMP-034 MaskedValue, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge and CMP-176 AccountKeyRow variants. Hard-to-reach states are produced with the E27-Q01 fixtures.

Findings are classified by WCAG success criterion (e.g. 1.4.1 Use of Colour, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 4.1.3 Status Messages) so the report is reviewable against the standard rather than against taste. Where an issue is a design defect rather than an implementation defect, it is routed back as a design ticket and noted in the E27-D07 drift report.

The exploratory charters use session-based test management: a stated charter, a time box, committed notes, and a debrief with the epic's engineers within one working day.

## Test plan
Automated cases (axe-core in the Playwright suite) become part of the E27-Q02 suite so they run continuously afterwards. The manual passes are evidenced with recordings or annotated transcripts. Re-test after fixes is mandatory and recorded; the ticket cannot close on "fixed, presumed working".

## Security notes
Charter 1 is deliberately an abuse-case exercise and its findings are shared with E27-X02: an accessibility affordance that exposes secret material (a tooltip, an autofill, a copy-to-clipboard on the wrong field, an aria-label containing a value) is a security defect first and an a11y note second, and is raised at P0.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility deliverable for the epic. Target: zero serious/critical axe violations, all six screens keyboard-complete, all state changes announced, contrast measured and passing, reflow at 320 CSS px verified.

## Performance notes
The audit records any state where an assistive-technology announcement lags the visual update by more than a second, since a live region that fires late on a safety verdict is a defect in practice even when technically conformant.

## Observability
Defects are filed with the axe rule id or WCAG criterion, the screen id, the state and the reproduction fixture. The report's summary counts feed the epic's quality rollup used at the R3 gate.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e27/` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Every listed case executed with a recorded pass/fail result and evidence; defects raised with exact reproduction steps and fixtures.
- [ ] Automated cases added to the CI suite and green on `main` on two consecutive runs.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 defects for E27; P2s triaged with named owners and target sprints.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment recorded on the epic E27.

## Dependencies
Blocked by all five implementation stories (**E27-S01**..**E27-S05**) - the screens must exist to be audited - and by **E27-D05**, which supplies the expected-announcement script that gives the manual pass a pass criterion.

## Branch
`chore/e27-a11y-audit` - report and automated a11y specs; fixes land on the owning story branches.

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#7-r3--trading-on-demo` - E27 scope line (34 pts, S14-S15), R3 exit criteria #9 and #10, quality gates (SS7.4), key dates (SS7.5)

title: Assemble the E27 regression pack and record QA sign-off for the epic
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS2.2 requires an epic-level regression and exploratory pass, recorded, before an epic may close - "not just child-ticket QA". E27 is additionally named in the R3 gate: roadmap SS7.3 exit criteria #9 and #10 are about this epic's behaviour, and SS7.4 requires QA and Security sign-off before the train closes on 2027-06-18.

This ticket is the closing gate. It consolidates what the other QA tickets produced into a durable regression pack that later trains re-run, executes the epic-level end-to-end pass across all ten ACCT stories in one sitting, and records the sign-off that lets E27 move to Done and unblocks the downstream epics that declared E27 as a dependency (E28, E29, E39, E42).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Regression pack** at `qa/regression/e27/`: the subset of `E27-TC-nnn` cases that must be re-run before every release, split into an automated tier (already in the E27-Q02 suite) and a manual tier (the cases that cannot be automated safely - step-up with a real authenticator, the KEK-loss drill, anything requiring the real exchange). Each manual case has an estimated execution time so release planning can budget it.
- **Epic-level end-to-end pass** executed once in a single session on the demo environment, in the order an owner would actually do it: register main and a sub-account; import and verify keys for both; observe health and balances; change leverage; rotate one key with overlap; let the policy reminder fire by clock manipulation; mark a key compromised; revoke it; disable one account and delete another; confirm the audit trail contains every step with the actor, and that no secret appears anywhere in the trail, the logs or the exported support bundle.
- **Traceability closure**: a matrix showing each of US-ACCT-001..010 with its evidence - the automated spec id, the manual case id, or both - and a statement that no Must/Should story is untested.
- **Defect status report**: all E27 defects with state, severity and disposition; confirmation of zero open P0/P1; P2s listed with owners and target sprints.
- **Cross-check against the runbooks** from E27-T05: the operator runbook's steps are executed literally by someone who did not write them, and any step that does not work as written is a defect against E27-T05.
- **QA sign-off comment** on the epic E27, naming the evidence, the residual risks and the explicit statement that R3 exit criteria #9 and #10 are demonstrated.

## Out of scope
- New test authoring - this ticket consolidates and executes rather than invents, except where the epic-level pass exposes a gap, which is then filled here.
- Security sign-off, which is E27-X04, and design sign-off, which is E27-D07; both are separate signatures on the same epic.
- Performance re-measurement (E27-Q03 owns the numbers; this ticket only confirms nothing regressed since).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every ACCT story has recorded evidence
  When the traceability closure matrix is reviewed
  Then each of US-ACCT-001 to US-ACCT-010 has at least one executed case with an evidence link, and none is marked untested or deferred

Scenario: The epic-level pass is done end to end, not piecemeal
  Given the full owner journey is executed in one session on demo
  Then every step succeeds or fails with a recorded defect, and the audit trail afterwards contains an entry for each state-changing step with the correct actor and no secret material

Scenario: The gate criteria are demonstrated, not asserted
  Given R3 exit criteria #9 (KEK separation) and #10 (withdrawal-enabled keys refused)
  When the sign-off comment is written
  Then it links to the restore-drill evidence for #9 and the rejection evidence for #10, both produced in this train, and dated

Scenario: The runbook works for someone who did not write it
  Given an engineer unfamiliar with the epic follows docs/ops/runbooks for rotation and compromise verbatim
  Then they complete both procedures without asking a question, and every deviation found is raised as a defect against E27-T05

Scenario: Sign-off is refused when defects remain
  Given an open P1 defect exists against E27
  When sign-off is attempted
  Then it is withheld and the epic stays out of Done until the defect is closed or formally accepted by the Owner in writing

## Technical notes / design
The regression pack is designed to be re-run by someone with no prior context: each case states its fixture, its preconditions and its expected result in full. Cases that depend on the calendar (key-age policy) use documented clock manipulation on the demo stack rather than waiting, and the method is written down.

The support-bundle check deserves specific mention: the bundle is generated during the epic-level pass and grepped for the known test secrets, the KEK, key-id prefixes beyond the masked form and the deployment egress IP. This closes the loop on the ADR-0009 validation item at the level a user would actually trigger it.

Sign-off is a written artefact, not a status change: a comment naming what was executed, on which build (commit SHA), against which environment, with the residual-risk list. That is what the R3 PRR consumes.

## Test plan
Execution of the full regression pack against the release-candidate build, with evidence captured per case. Any case that cannot be executed is escalated rather than skipped. The pack is re-run in full at the R3 gate and thereafter at every release per `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Security notes
The sign-off explicitly states whether any secret material was observed anywhere during the epic-level pass - in the UI, an API response, a log, a metric label, a trace, an error body or the support bundle - with "none observed, checked in the following places" enumerated. A vague sign-off is not acceptable for this epic. Security sign-off remains separate (E27-X04) and neither substitutes for the other. Classification: Internal.

## Accessibility notes
The regression pack carries forward the accessibility cases that must not regress (keyboard completion of each flow, the withdrawal verdict announced as text) so later releases re-check them without re-running the full E27-Q04 audit.

## Performance notes
Confirms the budgets measured in E27-Q03 still hold on the release-candidate build with a light re-run of the steady-state script; a regression here blocks sign-off.

## Observability
Sign-off records the epic's final metric and audit-event inventory, confirming that each documented event fired at least once during the epic-level pass - a documented-but-never-emitted audit event is a defect found here.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e27/` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Every listed case executed with a recorded pass/fail result and evidence; defects raised with exact reproduction steps and fixtures.
- [ ] Automated cases added to the CI suite and green on `main` on two consecutive runs.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 defects for E27; P2s triaged with named owners and target sprints.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment recorded on the epic E27.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-Q02**, **E27-Q03** and **E27-Q04** (their outputs are the evidence being consolidated) and by **E27-T05** (the runbooks this pass executes literally). Gates the epic's Done transition together with E27-X04 and E27-D07.

title: Produce the STRIDE threat model for accounts, sub-accounts and the API-key vault
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes a STRIDE threat model per epic non-negotiable, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS2.1 makes it default-on for any epic touching auth, keys, OMS or money movement, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7.4 names E27 explicitly in the R3 security gate: "STRIDE for E27, E29, E34, E35, E39, E42 - all Critical/High closed".

E27 is the epic that holds credentials capable of moving real money. ADR-0009 already fixes the architecture (KEK outside the database, DEK per record, decryption narrowed to the exchange adapter, withdrawal always off, IP allowlist mandatory), but an ADR is a decision, not an analysis: it does not enumerate the ways the decision can be defeated in implementation. This ticket does that enumeration before the vault is built, so the controls land as code rather than as retrofits.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Threat model document at `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md`, linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, containing:
  - **System decomposition**: a data-flow diagram (mermaid) covering credential intake (SCR-126 -> `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys`), storage (`api_keys.secret_enc`, `dek_ref`, `kek_version`), borrow (credential broker -> exchange adapter -> signed request), verification (`/keys/{keyId}/test`, the nightly job), rotation (`/keys/{keyId}/rotate`, `api_key_rotations`), revocation (`DELETE /keys/{keyId}`), and the read paths (`GET /exchange-accounts`, the `wallet` WS topic, SCR-079, SCR-125, SCR-128).
  - **Trust boundaries** marked against `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS2.2: browser -> API, API -> Postgres, API -> host KEK source, API -> Bybit, and the WSL/host boundary that ADR-0009 depends on.
  - **STRIDE enumeration per element and per flow**, each threat with likelihood, impact, the existing control, the gap, and a concrete mitigation ticket. At minimum: **S** - session fixation on the admin routes, a forged step-up, impersonating the host KEK launcher; **T** - ciphertext substitution (mitigated by the GCM tag), tampering with `permission_snapshot` to fake a passed verification, mutating `env`/`exchange_uid` after creation, tampering with the egress IP determination; **R** - a key action without an audit row, audit-chain break, an operator denying a revoke; **I** - database dump, log line, trace attribute, metric label, exception body, support bundle, core dump, browser autofill/password manager, screenshot, clipboard, the `key_id_masked` prefix being over-long; **D** - self-check storm consuming the per-UID rate budget and starving order placement, KEK unavailability halting trading, revoking the last key of an account with open positions; **E** - a manager reaching an account outside their grant via REST or a raw WS frame, `keys:manage` leaking into a non-owner role, the development `CV_KEK_SOURCE=file` path reaching a live deployment.
  - **Abuse cases** written as adversary narratives: a stolen laptop with the Postgres volume; a malicious or coerced account manager; a compromised dependency that reads process memory; an attacker with a valid viewer session hunting for a reveal endpoint; an operator tricked into pasting a live key into a demo-bound account.
  - **Risk register updates** in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` for any new risk surfaced.
  - A **control checklist** naming, for each accepted control, the automated check that proves it (unit test, contract test, CI rule, DAST rule) and the ticket that implements it - E27-T02, E27-T03, E27-X02, E27-X03 or a new ticket.
- A kickoff and a review session with the Architect, DevSecOps and the backend lead for the epic; decisions recorded in the document.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the mitigations - those are the referenced engineering tickets.
- Threat modelling the OMS (E29), fan-out (E34) or auth itself (E09); this model consumes E09's conclusions rather than repeating them.
- The penetration test, which happens before Live enablement in R4 (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element and flow is analysed
  When docs/security/threat-models/E27.md is reviewed by the Architect
  Then every element and every data flow in the DFD has all six STRIDE categories considered, with each either analysed or explicitly marked not-applicable with a one-line reason

Scenario: Each threat has a control with a test
  When the control checklist is reviewed
  Then every Critical and High threat names a mitigation ticket and an automated check that would fail if the control were removed, and no Critical or High is closed with documentation alone

Scenario: The development KEK source cannot reach live
  Given the threat "CV_KEK_SOURCE=file used in a live deployment"
  When the mitigation is verified
  Then a start-up assertion refuses to boot when CV_KEK_SOURCE=file and CV_ENV=live, and a unit test asserts that refusal

Scenario: The model is finished before the vault is built
  Given E27-T02 is the credential broker implementation
  When E27-T02 enters In Progress
  Then this threat model is at least in review with its Critical/High list stable, and E27-T02's design reflects it

## Technical notes / design
The model follows the four-question frame (what are we building; what can go wrong; what are we going to do about it; did we do a good job) with STRIDE-per-element as the enumeration technique, matching `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Severity uses the security program's rating scale so findings are comparable across epics.

Two structural conclusions are expected to fall out and should be stated explicitly because later tickets depend on them: (1) the secret columns must never appear on any serialisable model - a structural control rather than a filtering control, because filtering fails open; (2) account scope must be derived server-side from the session on every request and every WS subscription, never accepted from the client, because the epic's highest-likelihood elevation-of-privilege path is a manager enumerating accounts.

The document is versioned in the repository and re-reviewed if the epic's scope changes; ADR-0009 gets an amendment note if the model contradicts any of its assumptions.

## Test plan
The deliverable is a document, verified by peer review rather than by execution. Its downstream verification is real: E27-X03 implements the RBAC matrix test the model demands, E27-X02 runs the review that confirms the controls exist in code, and E27-Q03's chaos scenarios exercise the denial-of-service and availability threats. A threat whose control has no test is treated as an open finding.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security deliverable. Data classification for the epic is fixed here: `secret_enc`, `enc_nonce`, `dek_ref` and the KEK are **Secret**; `exchange_uid`, `label`, `permission_snapshot`, balances and fee rates are **Confidential**; health states are **Internal**. Every later ticket in E27 cites this classification rather than re-deciding it.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. The model does, however, record the accessibility-adjacent disclosure paths (tooltips, aria-labels, clipboard, autofill) as information-disclosure threats, which E27-Q04 charter 1 then hunts for.

## Performance notes
The model records the denial-of-service threat quantitatively: the per-UID exchange rate budget from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS4.3, how much of it verification may consume, and the reserved share the order path must retain. E27-Q03 measures against those numbers.

## Observability
The model specifies the audit events that must exist for non-repudiation (`account.created`, `account.updated`, `account.tested`, `account.key_rotated`, `account.disabled`, `account.deleted`, `account.disabled_by_policy`, `admin.key_marked_compromised`, `admin.secrets_policy_changed`), that they must be hash-chained per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS3.10, and the security-relevant metrics that must exist for detection (failed verification counts, credential-borrow rate, KEK load failures).

- [ ] Findings logged in the security register with severity, owner and due date.

Blocked by **E27-K01** (the KEK custody decision is an input to the model's trust boundaries) and **E09** (auth, sessions, step-up and RBAC are the foundation this model builds on). Gates the design of E27-T02 and E27-T03.

title: Security-review the credential broker, verification pipeline and key lifecycle implementation
body:
## Context
ADR-0009's security properties are only real if the implementation preserves them. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a white-box security review per security-relevant feature, and roadmap SS7.4 requires "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes". This ticket is that review, performed by the Security engineer against the code as merged rather than against the design as intended.

The review's central question is narrow and answerable: can a plaintext credential, or the KEK, reach anywhere it should not - disk, logs, traces, metrics, error bodies, the support bundle, a core dump, a database dump, an API response, a WS frame, or the browser - and can any actor cause a key to be trusted when it should not be?

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Code review** of `services/api/candleviewer/credentials/` (broker, KEK loader, wrapper type), `candleviewer/admin/accounts.py` and `keyvault.py`, the verification pipeline from E27-T03, the rotation and revocation paths, the API routers for `/exchange-accounts*`, and the frontend key-intake and rotation features - reviewed against the E27-X01 control checklist item by item, with a written verdict per control.
- **Leak-assertion suite**, owned by Security and wired as a required CI check, implementing ADR-0009's validation item in depth: a crafted log line containing a known key value is asserted absent from stdout, log files, the `/metrics` endpoint, OpenTelemetry span attributes, every 4xx/5xx response body produced by the epic's routes, and the generated support bundle. Includes a test that the wrapper type's `__repr__`, `__str__`, `__format__` and pydantic `model_dump()` all return the mask, and a test that no SQLAlchemy model exposing `secret_enc`/`dek_ref` is reachable from any response schema.
- **Abuse-case execution** against the running demo stack, from the narratives in E27-X01: attempt to retrieve a secret through every route and WS topic the epic touches; attempt to promote a key that failed verification; attempt to tamper with `permission_snapshot` directly in the database and confirm the next self-check overrides rather than trusts it; attempt to mutate `env`/`exchange_uid` via `PATCH`; attempt to cause the app to treat a live key as demo; attempt to keep a revoked key usable by racing revoke against an in-flight borrow.
- **Static-analysis rules** committed and enabled: Semgrep rules that fail the build when the secret columns appear in a serialiser, when a credential-typed value is interpolated into an f-string or log call, and when `CV_KEK_SOURCE` is read outside the loader; a Bandit profile for the module; a secrets-scanning rule tuned to Bybit key shapes so a real key committed anywhere in the repository fails CI.
- **DAST**: OWASP ZAP authenticated scan configured for the `/api/v1/exchange-accounts*` routes with the epic's session and step-up flows scripted, run in the nightly job; findings triaged.
- **Dependency review** of anything new the epic introduced into the credential path, with a note on why each dependency is trusted there.
- Findings written to the security register with severity, owner and due date; a written sign-off verdict at the end.

## Out of scope
- Re-deriving the threat model (E27-X01) or re-running the RBAC matrix (E27-X03), though the review confirms both are in place.
- The full penetration test, which is R4 (E43).
- Fixing findings - each becomes a Bug on the owning implementation ticket, re-tested here.
- Reviewing profiles, the OMS or fan-out.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No path leaks a credential
  Given the leak-assertion suite runs against a build where a known secret has been stored
  When logs, metrics, traces, error bodies, the support bundle and a database dump are scanned
  Then the secret appears in none of them, and the suite fails the build if any future change makes it appear

Scenario: A failed verification cannot be promoted
  Given a candidate key that fails the withdrawal check
  When an operator attempts, through the API directly rather than the UI, to attach it or mark it primary
  Then the server refuses with validation_failed / key_withdraw_permission, nothing is persisted, and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Database-level tampering does not win
  Given permission_snapshot is edited directly in Postgres to claim withdrawal is disabled
  When the next self-check runs
  Then the live exchange response overrides the stored snapshot, the account is force-disabled for trading, and a critical alert is raised

Scenario: Revoke wins every race
  Given a credential borrow is in flight when the key is revoked
  When the race is executed repeatedly
  Then no signed request is issued with the revoked key after revocation completes, and the borrow either completes before revocation or fails cleanly

Scenario: Static analysis blocks a regression
  Given a developer adds secret_enc to a response model on a branch
  When CI runs
  Then the Semgrep rule fails the build with a message naming the rule and the file

## Technical notes / design
The review is checklist-driven against E27-X01 rather than impressionistic, and its output is a table: control, where it is implemented, how it was verified, verdict. Controls that exist only as prose are findings.

The race test for revocation is worth the effort because it is the class of bug that code review does not find: it is executed as a loop of several hundred iterations with the borrow and the revoke started from separate tasks, asserting the invariant "no signed request after revocation completes" holds every time. ADR-0009's principle that local deletion is authoritative means the test must also confirm the local delete happens even when the remote call fails.

Semgrep rules live in `.semgrep/e27-credentials.yml` and are owned by Security in CODEOWNERS, so they cannot be weakened without Security review - a rule an engineer can delete is not a control.

## Test plan
The review includes verifying the tests that other tickets claim: Security independently confirms that the coverage claimed on the credential broker is real (the branches that matter are exercised, not just the happy path) and that the contract tests actually assert the absence of secret fields rather than merely not asserting their presence.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security deliverable. It must end with an explicit verdict for the R3 gate: whether key handling in E27 is fit to proceed toward Live enablement, with residual risks named. Any Critical or High left open blocks the R3 gate per roadmap SS7.4. The review is also the prerequisite package for the R4 pen-test, so the artefacts are written to be handed to an external tester.

## Accessibility notes
The review covers the client-side disclosure surface that accessibility affordances can create - aria-labels, tooltips, clipboard, autofill, screenshots - handing findings to and taking findings from E27-Q04 charter 1. Secret inputs must be marked so password managers and autofill do not retain them, and this is verified in a real browser.

## Performance notes
The review confirms that security controls do not themselves create a denial-of-service path: the verification pipeline's exchange calls are budgeted, the leak-assertion suite does not run in the hot path, and audit writes on the key paths are bounded. Numbers come from E27-Q03.

## Observability
Confirms every security-relevant event from E27-X01 is emitted, hash-chained and complete: actor, account, key fingerprint (never the key), outcome and reason. Confirms that failed verifications and KEK load failures raise alerts that a human actually receives, by triggering one of each and observing the notification.

- [ ] All Critical/High findings closed before the R3 gate (roadmap SS7.4 Security gate: "STRIDE for E27 ... all Critical/High closed").
