title: Implement the RBAC and account-scope assertion matrix for every accounts and key route and topic
body:
## Context
E27 introduces the first surfaces where a non-owner user can see something money-related: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` marks the account routes with `x-rbac` permissions `accounts:read`, `accounts:write`, `keys:read` and `keys:manage`, with scope `granted_accounts` for reads and `none` (owner-only) for key management, and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS6.3 requires that private topics are account-scoped with out-of-scope requests silently narrowed and a wholly out-of-scope request rejected with `account_scope_denied`. The WS protocol document's own invariant table states: "Manager cannot subscribe to another manager's accounts, even by raw frame."

Elevation of privilege is the highest-likelihood threat in E27-X01's enumeration, and it is exactly the kind that a manual review misses once and nobody notices for a year. This ticket converts the permission matrix into an executable assertion that runs on every build.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A machine-readable matrix at `services/api/tests/security/rbac_matrix_accounts.yaml` enumerating, for every route and topic this epic introduces, the expected outcome for each of the three roles (Owner, Manager, Viewer) in each of three scope situations (granted account, non-granted account, non-existent account): `GET /exchange-accounts`, `POST /exchange-accounts`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}`, `GET|POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys`, `DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}`, `POST .../rotate`, `POST .../test`, `GET .../fee-rate`, `PATCH /positions/{positionId}/leverage`, and the WS topics `wallet` and `positions` as they relate to account scope.
- A parameterised test that executes the whole matrix against the running app with real sessions for each role, asserting the exact status code and error code - `403` with the documented problem type for REST, `account_scope_denied` for a wholly out-of-scope WS subscription, and silent narrowing with the effective list reported in `sub_ok.effective` for a partially out-of-scope one.
- **Enumeration-resistance assertions**: a non-granted account id and a non-existent account id must be indistinguishable to a Manager (same status, same body, comparable timing), so the API cannot be used to enumerate which accounts exist.
- **Step-up assertions**: every route the screen specs mark as step-up-gated (`account.created|updated`, key attach, rotate, revoke, disable, delete) refuses without a fresh step-up and succeeds with one, and a step-up token for one action cannot be replayed for another.
- **Coverage guard**: a test that fails when a route tagged `exchange-accounts` exists in `22-api-openapi.yaml` but has no row in the matrix, so a new endpoint cannot be added without declaring its RBAC expectations.
- Documentation of the matrix in `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md` as the evidence for the elevation-of-privilege mitigations.

## Out of scope
- Implementing RBAC itself - roles, permissions, `user_account_access` and the scope resolver are E09's; this ticket asserts their correct application to E27's surface.
- Routes belonging to other epics (profiles E28, orders E29), though the matrix pattern is intended for reuse there.
- UI-level permission hiding, which is a usability affordance and never the enforcement point.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A manager cannot reach a non-granted account
  Given a manager session with access to account A only
  When the manager requests GET /exchange-accounts/{B} for an account B they were not granted
  Then the response is 403 with the documented problem type, the body reveals nothing about whether B exists, and the attempt is audited

Scenario: A manager cannot manage keys at all
  Given a manager session with access to account A
  When the manager attempts POST /exchange-accounts/{A}/keys
  Then the request is refused because keys:manage is owner-only with scope none, regardless of the account grant

Scenario: A raw WS frame cannot widen scope
  Given a manager session granted account A
  When the client sends a sub frame naming accounts A and B on the wallet topic
  Then the subscription succeeds narrowed to A only, sub_ok.effective reports A alone, and no frame for B is ever delivered

Scenario: A wholly out-of-scope subscription is an error, not a silent no-op
  Given the same manager session
  When the client subscribes to wallet for account B only
  Then the server responds with account_scope_denied

Scenario: A new endpoint cannot skip the matrix
  Given a developer adds a route tagged exchange-accounts to the OpenAPI document
  When CI runs
  Then the coverage guard fails until a matrix row with expected outcomes for all three roles is added

Scenario: Step-up cannot be replayed across actions
  Given a fresh step-up completed for a key rotation
  When the same step-up token is presented for an account deletion
  Then the deletion is refused and requires its own step-up

## Technical notes / design
The matrix is data, not code, so it is reviewable by the Security engineer without reading Python, and its diff in a pull request is legible - "this route became readable by managers" is visible at a glance. The test harness seeds three users with the three roles and a fixed grant map in `user_account_access`, then walks the matrix.

Timing indistinguishability is asserted loosely (order-of-magnitude, not constant-time) because the goal is to prevent trivial enumeration, not to defend against a lab-grade side channel; the ticket states that limit explicitly rather than implying a stronger guarantee than it delivers.

WS assertions run against a real gateway connection rather than a mocked subscription manager, because the bug class this targets - demand aggregation that forgets to re-check scope - lives in the integration, not the unit.

## Test plan
The matrix test is the test. It runs in the `security` CI job on every PR and in the nightly full suite. Manual verification during E27-X02 spot-checks three matrix rows by hand to confirm the harness is not vacuously passing - a matrix test that asserts nothing is a common and dangerous failure mode, so the harness additionally includes a self-check that deliberately flips one expectation and confirms the suite fails.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* a security control. It addresses the elevation-of-privilege and information-disclosure branches of E27-X01 directly, and it is the standing regression guard for them. Data classification: the matrix itself is Internal; the test users' credentials are test-only and generated per run. Requires Security-engineer review and sign-off.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. The matrix does record which controls the UI is expected to hide for each role, so that E27-Q04's keyboard pass can confirm a hidden control is genuinely absent from the accessibility tree rather than merely visually hidden.

## Performance notes
The matrix run adds bounded time to CI (target under 90 seconds for the full walk); it is parameterised so it can be sharded if it grows. Scope resolution itself must stay off the hot path - the test records the per-request scope-resolution overhead so a regression into a per-request database walk is visible.

## Observability
Every denied attempt emits an audit event with the actor, the target account and the reason, so repeated denials are detectable; the test asserts those events exist. A metric counting authorisation denials by route and role is added so a spike is alertable - an attacker probing scope should be visible in Grafana, not only in a log file nobody reads.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings logged in the security register with severity, owner and due date.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings closed before the R3 gate (roadmap SS7.4 Security gate: "STRIDE for E27 ... all Critical/High closed").
- [ ] Every agreed control encoded as an automated check (CI rule, unit test, contract test or DAST rule), not only as prose.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer; the STRIDE document is stored at `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md` and linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-X01** (which demands this control), **E27-T03** (the key routes must exist to be asserted) and **E27-S01** (accounts and grants must exist to scope against). Relies on E09's roles, permissions, `user_account_access` and step-up.

title: Run the key-compromise, restore and rotation drills and record the epic security sign-off
body:
## Context
ADR-0009 lists three validations that are only meaningful when actually executed: the security log-leak test, a **restore drill** ("restore a database backup on a machine without the KEK and confirm no key can be decrypted and the app refuses trading mode") and a **rotation drill** ("full 90-day rotation executed once before Live enablement (R4) as a PRR item"). Roadmap SS7.3 exit criterion #9 requires KEK separation to be *demonstrated*, not designed. `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` makes drill evidence a PRR input.

This ticket executes those drills, adds the compromise drill that the incident runbook implies, and produces the Security sign-off that - together with QA (E27-Q05) and design (E27-D07) - closes E27.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Restore drill**: take a real Postgres backup of the demo deployment, restore it on a clean machine with no access to the KEK, and prove that (a) no `api_keys` row decrypts, (b) the application refuses to enter trading mode, (c) the failure message is the documented degraded-mode banner rather than a stack trace. Evidence: terminal transcript, screenshots, and a written statement that the backup alone is unusable - the intended property.
- **Rotation drill**: execute a complete rotation on a demo account following `docs/ops/runbooks` from E27-T05 verbatim - create the replacement, verify it, overlap, confirm traffic moved, retire the old key - measuring elapsed time per stage, confirming no open order was cancelled and no private stream dropped an update, and confirming `api_key_rotations` records the full history.
- **KEK rotation drill**: bump `kek_version`, run the re-wrap job across all DEKs, confirm every key still decrypts and no ciphertext changed, and confirm `ix_api_keys_kek` drives the job to completion with a resumable checkpoint.
- **Compromise drill**: simulate a suspected compromise end to end - mark a key compromised from SCR-128, confirm the account's trading halts immediately, rules scoped to it disarm, the key is revoked locally even when the Bybit call is forced to fail, positions are surfaced for the flatten-or-leave decision, and the audit trail reconstructs the whole incident from `prev_hash`/`row_hash` with no gap. Time the drill and record the detection-to-contained interval.
- **Egress-IP and allowlist verification**: confirm the deployment's egress IP determination is correct and that a mismatch is detected and surfaced with the copy-pasteable current IP (US-ACCT-003); confirm the manual Bybit allowlist step is documented in the VPS migration runbook, since ADR-0009 records that it cannot be automated.
- **Sign-off artefact** at `docs/security/signoffs/E27.md`: the verdict, the evidence index, residual risks with owners, and the explicit statement of readiness for the R3 gate and of the package handed to the R4 pen-test.

## Out of scope
- Fixing anything the drills break - raised as Bugs against the owning tickets and re-drilled.
- The R4 penetration test itself (E43) and Live enablement gating (E44); this ticket only prepares their inputs.
- Drills for the OMS, fan-out or risk caps, which belong to their own epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A stolen database is useless
  Given a Postgres backup restored on a machine with no KEK
  When the application is started against it in trading mode
  Then no api_keys row decrypts, the app enters degraded read-only mode with the documented banner, every trading route refuses, and the transcript is captured as evidence for R3 exit criterion #9

Scenario: Rotation is boring
  Given the rotation runbook is followed verbatim on a demo account with an open order
  When the drill completes
  Then the new key is primary, the old key is revoked, the open order was never cancelled, no private stream gap was observed, and total elapsed time is recorded

Scenario: KEK rotation rewraps without touching ciphertext
  Given kek_version is bumped and the re-wrap job runs
  When it completes
  Then every key still decrypts, the ciphertext columns are byte-identical to before, and interrupting the job midway and restarting it produces the same end state

Scenario: A compromise is contained in minutes and reconstructible
  Given the compromise drill is executed with the Bybit revoke call forced to fail
  When the drill completes
  Then the key is gone locally regardless, trading for that account halted, scoped rules disarmed, the operator was told to revoke at Bybit with the exact error shown, and the audit chain verifies with no gap

Scenario: Sign-off is specific
  When docs/security/signoffs/E27.md is written
  Then it names each drill with its date, build SHA and evidence link, lists residual risks with owners, and states plainly whether E27 is fit to proceed toward Live enablement

## Technical notes / design
Drills are executed by the Security engineer with DevSecOps, on the demo deployment, following the runbooks literally - the runbook being wrong is one of the outcomes this ticket is looking for, and any deviation is filed against E27-T05 rather than silently corrected in the moment.

The restore drill uses a genuinely separate machine (or a container with no host credential access) rather than an environment variable unset on the same host, because the property being demonstrated is custody separation, and testing it by simply hiding the key from oneself proves nothing.

The compromise drill is timed because incident response is a latency problem: the recorded detection-to-contained interval becomes the baseline the R4 readiness review compares against, and it is the number the Owner actually cares about when deciding whether the response plan is adequate.

All drills are re-run before Live enablement in R4; this ticket establishes the procedure and the first evidence, and the runbook records the re-run schedule.

## Test plan
Each drill has an explicit pass criterion stated above and evidence captured in `docs/security/drills/e27/`. Failed drills are re-run after fixes; a drill is never signed off on a partial pass. The audit-chain verification uses the chain verifier from E09 rather than manual inspection.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security deliverable and the epic's closing security gate. Residual risks expected to be recorded rather than eliminated: KEK availability remains a single point of failure for starting the service (accepted in ADR-0009 with an owner-held offline backup); the Bybit IP allowlist remains a manual step; the 48-hour new-key restriction constrains how fast an emergency rotation can complete, which the compromise runbook must state honestly. The drills must never be run against `live` - a guard and a written pre-flight check enforce this.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - operational drills. The compromise drill does confirm that the blocking degraded-mode banner is announced to assistive technology, since it is the one state a user must not miss.

## Performance notes
Records the measured durations: rotation total against the SCR-127 <=10 s target for the in-app portion, re-wrap job throughput, degraded-mode entry time on KEK loss, and detection-to-contained for the compromise drill. These feed the R3 PRR.

## Observability
Confirms the drills are visible in telemetry: KEK load failures, credential-borrow failures, verification failures and authorisation denials all appear in Grafana and fire the configured alerts during the drills, with the alert actually reaching the owner's notification channel - an alert that fires into a void is a finding.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings logged in the security register with severity, owner and due date.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings closed before the R3 gate (roadmap SS7.4 Security gate: "STRIDE for E27 ... all Critical/High closed").
- [ ] Every agreed control encoded as an automated check (CI rule, unit test, contract test or DAST rule), not only as prose.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer; the STRIDE document is stored at `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md` and linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-X02** and **E27-X03** (the controls must be reviewed and asserted before drilling them), **E27-T05** (the runbooks being executed verbatim) and **E27-Q03** (which produced the KEK-loss chaos scenario this ticket reuses). Together with E27-Q05 and E27-D07 it gates the epic's Done transition.

`chore/e27-security-drills` - drill evidence and sign-off documents; runbook corrections land on E27-T05's branch.
